paper_title: A Survey on LoRa Networking: Research Problems, Current Solutions and Open Issues
context_brief: Long-range LoRa communication without heavy chip modifications
original_question: How can the reliable communication range of LoRa links be improved without heavy modifications to commercially available LoRa radio chips? The problem includes enabling gateways to make use of weak long-range signals that they may be able to detect but not decode, while avoiding approaches that depend on USRP radios, ambiguous commercial-chip implementation paths, backscatter-specific modifications, or other substantial hardware changes.
self_contained_problem:
Consider the LoRa (Long Range) wireless communication system, in which low-power end devices transmit Chirp Spread Spectrum (CSS) modulated packets to gateways over distances of several kilometers. A LoRa gateway equipped with a commercially available LoRa transceiver chip can detect the presence of an incoming chirp packet whose received signal strength lies above its detection threshold but below the threshold needed to correctly demodulate and decode the payload; such packets are normally discarded.

Design a reliable communication scheme that extends the effective decoding range of LoRa uplinks under the following constraints:

1. End devices use unmodified, commercially available LoRa radio chips and standard CSS-modulated transmissions (no custom backscatter hardware, no replacement of the chip's PHY-layer signal generation, and no use of software-defined radios such as USRPs at the end-device side).
2. Gateways may be augmented only by lightweight, well-specified auxiliary processing (for example, additional digital signal processing in firmware/cloud, multi-antenna combining, or coordinated multi-gateway reception), but must not require replacing the commercial LoRa chip itself or rely on implementation paths whose realizability on commercial chips is unclear.
3. The scheme must enable the recovery of payload bits from packets whose per-gateway SNR is below the standard LoRa decoding threshold, by exploiting weak-but-detectable signals (e.g., through joint/coherent combining across multiple gateways or antennas, denoising, or comparable techniques).

Specify the signal-processing and networking algorithm, prove or empirically establish that it strictly enlarges the decodable range compared with a single standard LoRa gateway, and quantify the achievable range gain and energy/battery-life impact while preserving compatibility with unmodified commercial LoRa end devices.
category_tag: LoRa wireless communication and signal decoding
status_search_result: Several systems have substantially advanced this problem since it was posed. Charm performs coherent combining of weak signals across multiple gateways; MALoRa uses gateway antenna diversity to combine signals before standard LoRa demodulation; and SRLoRa applies neural super-resolution-style denoising across multiple gateways to decode signals well below the single-gateway SNR threshold. These approaches keep commercial LoRa end devices unmodified and report multi-fold range and battery improvements. However, several proposed gateway-side solutions still rely on SDR-based gateway prototypes (e.g., USRP N210), so a fully commercial-chip, end-to-end deployment satisfying all stated constraints remains only partially achieved.

paper_title: A Survey on LoRa Networking: Research Problems, Current Solutions and Open Issues
context_brief: LoRa link-quality and coverage estimation models
original_question: How can LoRa networking obtain mathematical models and systems for estimating link quality and communication coverage across diverse deployment environments, including open-air locations, concrete- or steel-obstructed locations, homes, hospitals, schools, forests, line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight conditions, signal attenuation, propagation losses, fading, and anisotropic coverage caused by dynamic and static obstacles in different directions?
category_tag: Wireless channel modeling and coverage estimation
status_search_result: Several works have proposed partial solutions: remote-sensing-based automated link-quality estimation combining multispectral imagery with the Okumura-Hata model (Demetri et al., IPSN 2019); a First Fresnel Zone log-normal shadowing model classifying mediums along the path; FLog and related orchard-specific models; and SVM/kernel-based machine-learning estimators using RSSI, SNR, and PRR. These address aspects of anisotropy and heterogeneous environments, but a unified, rigorously validated mathematical framework with provable accuracy across all deployment scenarios (indoor, NLOS, forested, urban, transitional) remains an open research direction.

paper_title: A Survey on LoRa Networking: Research Problems, Current Solutions and Open Issues
context_brief: Efficient LoRa channel coding for packet loss
original_question: How can LoRa use efficient channel-coding techniques to recover corrupted or lost data without the limitations of existing redundancy-based approaches, including inability to handle bursty packet loss, increased memory and decoding complexity, higher latency, and extra transmissions that increase interference and collisions?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a low-power wide-area wireless network in which end devices transmit short packets to a gateway over a noisy channel that exhibits both random bit errors and bursty packet losses (entire packets dropped in consecutive bursts). Each device is severely constrained in memory, computation, energy, and tolerable latency, and any retransmission contributes to channel interference and collisions.

A baseline application-layer redundancy scheme works as follows. To transmit an information sequence of packets x_1, x_2, ..., x_n, each transmitted packet y_k carries x_k together with a linear combination over GF(2) of a window of the W previous information packets {x_{k-1}, ..., x_{k-W}} (with coefficients chosen by some generator). The receiver recovers lost packets by Gaussian elimination on the resulting banded generator matrix. This scheme has the following drawbacks: (i) it requires buffering the previous W packets at the encoder, (ii) the banded structure of the generator matrix prevents constructing an LT-code-like degree distribution, (iii) Gaussian-elimination decoding has high complexity, (iv) it does not effectively recover bursty losses, and (v) any added redundancy or retransmission increases collisions.

Problem. Design a channel/erasure coding scheme for such a network, together with an encoding and decoding algorithm, that simultaneously satisfies the following requirements:

1. Recovers from both isolated bit corruption and bursty packet erasures of length up to B with probability at least 1 − ε, for prescribed B and ε.
2. Uses encoder memory o(W) and per-packet encoding work O(1) (or at most polylogarithmic in n).
3. Admits a decoding algorithm whose time and space complexity are strictly lower than Gaussian elimination on a banded n × n matrix (e.g., near-linear in n).
4. Achieves end-to-end latency bounded by a constant number of packet intervals, without requiring feedback-driven retransmission.
5. Adds asymptotically less redundancy overhead than the baseline window scheme while matching or exceeding its packet-recovery rate, so that the offered traffic load (and hence collision probability) is not increased.

Provide such a code construction and prove the above properties, or prove that no scheme can simultaneously achieve (1)–(5) under the stated resource constraints.
status_search_result: The problem of designing a channel-coding scheme for LoRa that overcomes the limitations of redundancy-based application-layer codes (e.g., DaRe) — bursty-loss vulnerability, memory and decoding complexity, latency, and increased collisions — remains an active research area. Surveys and recent works continue to list it as an open issue, and proposed schemes (e.g., variants of fountain/LT codes, network coding, and FEC for LoRa) address subsets of the requirements but no single solution is established as fully satisfactory.

paper_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
original_question: In solar-wind turbulence at ion and electron kinetic scales, what is the physical nature of the fluctuations, and through which collisionless plasma mechanisms are those fluctuations dissipated? This question asks for a theory that can distinguish which competing collisionless processes are active at ion and electron scales and explain how they determine the observed kinetic-scale turbulent cascade and dissipation.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a weakly collisional, magnetized plasma such as the solar wind, modeled by the Vlasov–Maxwell system for ion and electron distribution functions f_s(x,v,t) (s ∈ {i,e}) coupled to electromagnetic fields (E,B). Assume a turbulent state in which energy injected at large (magnetohydrodynamic) scales cascades to smaller scales, crossing the ion kinetic scales (ion gyroradius ρ_i and ion inertial length d_i) and continuing down to the electron kinetic scales (ρ_e, d_e), where it is ultimately converted into particle internal energy (heating) by collisionless mechanisms.

Candidate collisionless dissipation/cascade mechanisms that may operate simultaneously include: (i) linear and nonlinear Landau damping on ions and electrons; (ii) cyclotron (ion or electron) resonant damping; (iii) stochastic ion heating by low-frequency, large-amplitude fluctuations; (iv) magnetic reconnection in current sheets formed by the cascade; (v) dissipation in coherent structures such as current sheets and vortices; (vi) wave–particle interactions associated with kinetic Alfvén waves, whistler waves, and ion-Bernstein modes.

Problem. Develop a predictive theory of the kinetic-scale turbulent cascade in such a plasma that:
(a) Determines, from the plasma parameters (e.g. ion and electron plasma betas β_i, β_e, ion-to-electron temperature ratio T_i/T_e, and the angle θ between the local mean magnetic field and the cascade wavevector), the physical nature of the fluctuations at sub-ion scales (k ρ_i ≳ 1) and at sub-electron scales (k ρ_e ≳ 1) — in particular, the relative weight of kinetic Alfvén-wave-like, whistler-like, and non-wavelike (e.g. coherent structure) fluctuations and their anisotropy in k-space.
(b) Identifies which of the candidate collisionless mechanisms above dominates the conversion of fluctuation energy into ion and electron heating in each regime, and quantifies the resulting partition of energy between parallel and perpendicular ion heating, electron heating, and any non-thermal particle acceleration.
(c) Predicts, as a function of these parameters, the spectral indices, spectral break scales, and amplitude ratios of magnetic, electric, and density fluctuations in the kinetic range, in a manner falsifiable by comparison with fully kinetic 3D-in-space, 3D-in-velocity Vlasov–Maxwell simulations and in situ spacecraft measurements.
status_search_result: This is a long-standing open question in space plasma physics. As of 2024–2026, no single theory uniquely identifies the nature of sub-ion and sub-electron scale fluctuations and their dominant collisionless dissipation channel; competing mechanisms (Landau damping, cyclotron damping, stochastic heating, reconnection, dissipation in coherent structures) are all observed to contribute under different conditions in Parker Solar Probe / MMS data and in 3D3V kinetic simulations. Recent reviews continue to describe it as unresolved.

paper_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
original_question: Do common turbulence features exist across independently performed 3D3V kinetic simulations using different numerical models, in a way that would demonstrate a genuine universality of kinetic-scale plasma turbulence? This requires separating robust, model-independent properties from differences caused by the large-scale driving, box size, filtering choices, reduced mass ratios, or the distinction between hybrid-kinetic and fully kinetic physics.
self_contained_problem:
Consider three-dimensional, three-velocity (3D3V) kinetic simulations of magnetized collisionless plasma turbulence in a periodic cubic domain, in which the plasma is driven at large scales and the turbulent cascade extends down to and below the ion kinetic scales (the ion gyroradius and ion inertial length). Different simulations may use different numerical models, including (i) fully kinetic Vlasov–Maxwell or particle-in-cell descriptions of both ions and electrons, and (ii) hybrid-kinetic descriptions in which ions are treated kinetically and electrons are treated as a (possibly massless) neutralizing fluid. Simulations may also differ in their large-scale driving mechanism, in box size, in spectral or hyper-dissipative filtering choices, and, in the fully kinetic case, in the (often artificially reduced) ion-to-electron mass ratio.

Define a "universal kinetic-scale turbulence feature" as a statistical property of the turbulent fluctuations at scales near and below the ion kinetic scales—such as the slope and shape of the magnetic, electric, and density power spectra, the spectral anisotropy with respect to the local mean magnetic field, intermittency exponents and structure functions, the distribution and morphology of current sheets and reconnection sites, the partitioning of energy dissipation between ions and electrons, and ion and electron velocity-space structures—whose value, up to controlled corrections, is independent of the choice of numerical model and of the above simulation parameters.

Problem. Determine whether such universal kinetic-scale turbulence features exist. More precisely:

(a) Identify a (possibly empty) set of statistical observables of 3D3V collisionless plasma turbulence whose values at sub-ion scales agree, within quantifiable error bars, across independently performed hybrid-kinetic and fully kinetic 3D3V simulations after suitable normalization (e.g., to the ion gyroradius, ion inertial length, and rms turbulent amplitude).

(b) For each such observable, separate the contribution that is robust under variation of the driving prescription, box size, filtering/dissipation, mass ratio, and hybrid-versus-fully-kinetic treatment from contributions that depend on these choices, and provide explicit scalings or bounds for the dependence on each parameter.

(c) Identify the underlying physical mechanism(s) (for example, magnetic reconnection in a sea of intermittent current sheets, kinetic Alfvén wave turbulence, stochastic heating, or Landau/cyclotron damping) responsible for the universal features identified in (a), and derive their statistical predictions from first principles in a way that reproduces the measured universal observables.
status_search_result: The question of universality of kinetic-scale plasma turbulence across different 3D3V simulation models is a long-standing open problem in plasma physics. Reviews and recent simulation studies (e.g., Cerri, Grošelj, Franci and collaborators) report broadly similar sub-ion spectral slopes and intermittency signatures in hybrid-kinetic and fully kinetic runs, but the underlying mechanism(s) and the precise model-independence remain unresolved and are still the subject of active investigation as of 2025–2026.

paper_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
original_question: What physical process causes the apparent contradiction between solar-wind observations, which show nearly scale-independent non-Gaussian turbulence statistics at sub-ion scales, and 3D kinetic simulations, which show excess kurtosis continuing to grow through the sub-ion range? More specifically, does collisionless reconnection limit the growth of sub-ion-scale kurtosis by disrupting sufficiently sheetlike intermittent structures, or are other mechanisms such as collisionless damping responsible for the observed saturation behavior?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a weakly collisional, magnetized plasma (such as the solar wind) modeled by the 3D-3V Vlasov–Maxwell system, in which a turbulent cascade transfers electromagnetic and kinetic-fluctuation energy from large MHD scales through the ion-Larmor scale (k ρ_i ~ 1) into the sub-ion range (k ρ_i ≫ 1, with k ρ_e ≲ 1). For a fluctuating field f (e.g., a magnetic-field component), define the scale-dependent increment δf(ℓ) = f(x+ℓ) − f(x) and the scale-dependent kurtosis

  K(ℓ) = ⟨δf(ℓ)^4⟩ / ⟨δf(ℓ)^2⟩^2,

which measures intermittency (Gaussian statistics give K=3). 

Empirically, in-situ solar-wind measurements indicate that K(ℓ) grows through the inertial range, reaches a maximum near the ion scale, and then becomes approximately scale-independent (saturates) throughout the sub-ion range. By contrast, fully kinetic 3D-3V simulations of driven plasma turbulence show K(ℓ) continuing to grow monotonically through the sub-ion range, with no such saturation.

Problem. Identify and justify the physical mechanism that produces the observed sub-ion-scale saturation of K(ℓ) in the solar wind but is either absent or insufficiently active in current 3D-3V kinetic simulations. In particular, decide between the following hypotheses (or formulate an alternative):

(a) Collisionless magnetic reconnection: sub-ion-scale intermittent structures are sufficiently sheet-like (large aspect ratio) to be tearing-unstable, and reconnection disrupts them before they reach smaller scales, thereby capping K(ℓ).

(b) Collisionless damping (e.g., Landau damping, cyclotron damping, stochastic heating) of fluctuations preferentially removes the most intermittent contributions to δf and saturates K(ℓ).

(c) A different mechanism, to be specified, with quantitative criteria for when it dominates.

A complete solution should provide a quantitative criterion (e.g., a threshold aspect ratio or damping rate compared with the nonlinear cascade rate) that determines saturation, and should explain why presently feasible 3D-3V simulations fail to reproduce it.
status_search_result: Recent literature (Bruno 2019; Roberts et al. 2022 Cluster multi-scale study; Parker Solar Probe sub-proton observations; HelioSwarm forecasts 2024) confirms that the saturation of sub-ion kurtosis is observed but its physical cause remains debated. Both reconnection-driven disruption of current sheets and collisionless damping continue to be proposed as candidate mechanisms, with no consensus resolution; the question is therefore still considered open.

paper_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
original_question: How is turbulent energy distributed in space and time in kinetic plasma turbulence? The question concerns the spatio-temporal organization of turbulent energy, rather than only its scale-by-scale spectrum, and is posed as a fundamental target for future multi-spacecraft measurements.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a collisionless or weakly collisional magnetized plasma whose dynamics are governed by the Vlasov–Maxwell system

  ∂_t f_s + v·∇_x f_s + (q_s/m_s)(E + v×B/c)·∇_v f_s = 0,    s ∈ {ions, electrons},
  ∇×B = (4π/c) J + (1/c) ∂_t E,    ∇×E = −(1/c) ∂_t B,
  ∇·E = 4π ρ,    ∇·B = 0,

with current and charge densities J = Σ_s q_s ∫ v f_s dv and ρ = Σ_s q_s ∫ f_s dv. Suppose the system is driven into a statistically stationary, fully developed turbulent state on a triply periodic three-dimensional spatial domain with three-dimensional velocity space (3D3V), with a mean magnetic field B_0 and turbulent fluctuations spanning scales from the magnetohydrodynamic range through the ion and electron kinetic ranges.

Define the local fluctuation energy density

  ε(x,t) = (|δB(x,t)|² + |δE(x,t)|²)/(8π) + Σ_s ∫ (m_s |v − u_s|² / 2) δf_s(x,v,t) dv,

and its space–time correlation/spectral structure via the four-dimensional Fourier transform ε̂(k,ω) of ε(x,t) (or, equivalently, of the underlying electromagnetic and particle-fluctuation fields).

Problem. Characterize quantitatively how turbulent energy is distributed jointly in physical space x and in time t (equivalently, in wavenumber k and frequency ω) in such a kinetic plasma turbulence state. In particular:

(a) Determine the joint (k,ω) energy distribution across the inertial, ion-kinetic, and electron-kinetic ranges, identifying which fraction of energy lies on linear wave dispersion surfaces ω = ω_α(k) (e.g. Alfvén, slow, kinetic Alfvén, whistler, ion-cyclotron branches) versus in non-wavelike, advected or coherent structures.

(b) Quantify the degree of spatial intermittency (volume-filling factor, multifractal scaling exponents of structure functions, and statistics of energy-dissipation surrogates) and the temporal intermittency (waiting-time and burst-duration distributions) of the energy density ε(x,t).

(c) Provide a predictive theory linking (a) and (b) to the driving parameters (plasma beta, ion-to-electron mass and temperature ratios, Alfvén Mach number, system size in units of ρ_i and d_i).

Give either a rigorous derivation, a closed phenomenological model with verified scaling laws, or a definitive numerical/observational characterization.
status_search_result: The spatio-temporal distribution of energy in kinetic plasma turbulence remains an active open research target. Recent reviews and mission-science papers (e.g., HelioSwarm, MMS multi-spacecraft analyses) explicitly list disentangling the joint (k,ω) energy distribution and characterizing intermittent spatial/temporal structure as outstanding goals not yet resolved by theory, simulation, or observation.

paper_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
original_question: What are the high-order statistics of fluctuations in kinetic plasma turbulence? In context, this means determining the intermittency-sensitive, non-Gaussian statistical structure of the turbulent fields at kinetic scales, beyond low-order spectral descriptions.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a fully ionized, weakly collisional, magnetized plasma in three spatial and three velocity dimensions, modeled by the Vlasov–Maxwell system

  ∂_t f_s + v·∇_x f_s + (q_s/m_s)(E + v×B/c)·∇_v f_s = 0,   s = i, e,
  ∂_t B = −c∇×E,    ∇×B = (4π/c) Σ_s q_s ∫ v f_s d^3v + (1/c) ∂_t E,
  ∇·B = 0,    ∇·E = 4π Σ_s q_s ∫ f_s d^3v,

driven into a statistically steady, strongly turbulent state with a mean magnetic field B_0 and characteristic ion gyroradius ρ_i and inertial length d_i. Let δψ_ℓ(x) = ψ(x+ℓ) − ψ(x) denote the spatial increment of a fluctuating field ψ ∈ {B, E, u_s, n_s, …} over a separation ℓ, and define the structure functions

  S_p^ψ(ℓ) = ⟨ |δψ_ℓ|^p ⟩,    p ≥ 1,

together with the scale-dependent kurtosis

  K^ψ(ℓ) = S_4^ψ(ℓ) / [S_2^ψ(ℓ)]^2,

and the standardized probability density functions P(δψ_ℓ / σ_ℓ).

Determine the high-order statistical structure of the turbulent fluctuations across the kinetic range ℓ ≲ ρ_i, d_i. Specifically:

(a) Characterize, for each field ψ, the scaling exponents ζ_p^ψ defined by S_p^ψ(ℓ) ∼ ℓ^{ζ_p^ψ} and the resulting multifractal spectrum, including any departure from a linear (self-similar) dependence ζ_p^ψ = p·ζ_1^ψ.

(b) Determine the scale dependence of K^ψ(ℓ) and of the full PDF P(δψ_ℓ/σ_ℓ) at sub-ion scales, including whether intermittency increases, saturates, or decreases as ℓ crosses ρ_i and d_i down to electron scales.

(c) Identify which fields (magnetic field components, electric field, ion and electron bulk velocities, densities) display the strongest non-Gaussian, intermittent behavior, and relate the observed higher-order statistics to the coherent structures (current sheets, vortices, reconnection sites) that produce them.
status_search_result: The high-order statistical structure of fluctuations at kinetic (sub-ion to electron) scales in collisionless plasma turbulence remains an active and unresolved area. Recent observational and numerical studies (MMS observations, 3D3V Vlasov simulations, hybrid PIC, HelioSwarm forecasts) report partial and sometimes conflicting results: some find a transition from intermittent to globally self-similar non-Gaussian statistics below ρ_i, while others report sustained intermittency tied to current sheets and reconnection, and electron-scale statistics are still poorly constrained. No complete theory of the multifractal spectrum and PDFs across the kinetic range exists.

paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
original_question: For networking datasets in which each sample contains fixed metadata together with an associated multivariate time series, can generative adversarial networks be used to create synthetic datasets that remain high-fidelity and generalize across downstream networking tasks without requiring substantial human expertise about workload characteristics or target tasks?
self_contained_problem:
Consider datasets of the form $\mathcal{D}=\{(m_i, x_i)\}_{i=1}^N$, where each sample consists of fixed-dimensional metadata $m_i \in \mathcal{M}$ (categorical and/or continuous attributes) and an associated multivariate time series $x_i = (x_i^{(1)}, \dots, x_i^{(T_i)})$ with $x_i^{(t)} \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and possibly variable length $T_i$. Such datasets arise in networking contexts (e.g., traffic measurements, system telemetry, user session traces) and exhibit features such as heterogeneous metadata distributions, long-range temporal correlations, multi-scale behavior, and strong coupling between metadata and time-series dynamics.

A generative model $G_\theta$ is said to produce a synthetic dataset $\widetilde{\mathcal{D}}$ that is "high-fidelity and task-generalizable" if, for a broad family $\mathcal{T}$ of downstream predictive or analytic tasks (each specified by a loss $\ell_T$ and an algorithm $A_T$ trained on a dataset), the performance gap
$$\Delta(T) = \big| \mathbb{E}[\ell_T(A_T(\widetilde{\mathcal{D}}))] - \mathbb{E}[\ell_T(A_T(\mathcal{D}))] \big|$$
is uniformly small over $T \in \mathcal{T}$, and if standard distributional fidelity metrics (marginal distributions of metadata, autocorrelation functions of time series, joint metadata–time-series statistics) on $\widetilde{\mathcal{D}}$ closely match those of $\mathcal{D}$.

Question: Does there exist a generative-adversarial-network–based procedure $G_\theta$, trained on $\mathcal{D}$ without task-specific supervision and without dataset-specific feature engineering or hand-crafted workload assumptions, such that for arbitrary networking datasets of the above form the resulting synthetic dataset $\widetilde{\mathcal{D}}$ is high-fidelity and task-generalizable in the sense above? Equivalently, characterize the conditions on $\mathcal{D}$, on the GAN architecture, and on the training procedure under which such universal high-fidelity, task-agnostic synthetic data generation is achievable.
category_tag: Generative adversarial networks for time-series synthesis
status_search_result: The question of building GAN-based synthetic data generators for networked time series that are high-fidelity and generalize across downstream tasks without manual feature engineering remains an active and open research area. Follow-up work (e.g., DoppelGANger and subsequent improvements) reports progress on specific datasets but acknowledges persistent challenges in privacy, mode coverage, long time-series fidelity, and cross-task generalization, indicating the broader question is not resolved.

paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
original_question: In GAN-based sharing of networked time-series datasets, can the generator support flexible notions of privacy in practice, and if so, under what training or generation configurations can those privacy notions be achieved?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the problem of releasing a synthetic version of a networked time-series dataset using a generative adversarial network (GAN). Formally, let $\mathcal{D} = \{(m_i, x_i)\}_{i=1}^n$ be a dataset where each record consists of a vector of metadata $m_i \in \mathcal{M}$ (e.g., per-object attributes) and an associated time series $x_i = (x_i^{(1)}, \dots, x_i^{(T)}) \in \mathcal{X}^T$. A GAN consists of a generator $G_\theta: \mathcal{Z} \to \mathcal{M} \times \mathcal{X}^T$ trained against a discriminator $D_\phi$ so that the induced distribution $P_{G_\theta}$ approximates the empirical distribution of $\mathcal{D}$.

A "flexible notion of privacy" refers to a family $\mathcal{P} = \{\Pi_\alpha\}_{\alpha \in A}$ of privacy specifications, where each $\Pi_\alpha$ may, for example, prescribe (i) a differential-privacy guarantee at level $(\varepsilon_\alpha, \delta_\alpha)$ for releasing $G_\theta$ or its samples, (ii) protection against membership inference for a specified subset of records, (iii) hiding of designated metadata attributes, or (iv) bounded leakage of designated time-series features, while preserving the joint distribution of the remaining attributes.

Determine whether there exist training procedures (loss functions, optimizers, noise-injection mechanisms, architectures) and sampling/generation configurations for $G_\theta$ such that, for a given specification $\Pi_\alpha \in \mathcal{P}$, the generator simultaneously (a) provably satisfies $\Pi_\alpha$ and (b) produces synthetic networked time-series samples whose statistical fidelity (in terms of marginal, temporal, and cross-record correlation metrics) is comparable to that of a non-private GAN trained on $\mathcal{D}$. Characterize the set of specifications $\Pi_\alpha$ for which such configurations exist, and describe explicit training/generation configurations achieving them.
category_tag: Generative adversarial networks for time-series privacy
status_search_result: The question is a broad open research direction concerning whether GANs can flexibly enforce diverse privacy notions when sharing networked time-series data. Subsequent work (e.g., DoppelGANger and follow-ups on differentially private time-series GANs) has explored differential-privacy training and selective attribute hiding, but no comprehensive characterization exists of which flexible privacy notions can be achieved with what configurations while retaining fidelity. The status is best described as open / actively researched.

paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
original_question: For networking and systems datasets that consist of time series and metadata rather than labeled images, how should GAN fidelity be evaluated when the standard, widely used GAN metrics were designed for image data and cannot be directly applied?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the problem of evaluating the fidelity of a generative adversarial network (GAN) trained on networked-systems data, where each sample is a pair $(M, X)$ consisting of a metadata vector $M \in \mathcal{M}$ (a mixture of categorical and continuous attributes) and a multivariate time series $X = (x_1, \ldots, x_T) \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times T}$ of variable or fixed length $T$. Let $P_{\text{real}}$ denote the (unknown) joint distribution over $(M, X)$ from which a finite training set is drawn, and let $P_{\text{gen}}$ denote the distribution induced by a trained generator $G$.

The most widely adopted GAN fidelity metrics (such as Inception Score and Fréchet Inception Distance) rely on features extracted by classifiers pretrained on large labeled image corpora and therefore do not apply to $(M, X)$ samples of this form.

Problem. Design a principled, general-purpose methodology for evaluating the fidelity of $P_{\text{gen}}$ relative to $P_{\text{real}}$ in this setting. Specifically:

(a) Propose a quantitative metric, or a finite collection of metrics, $\{\mu_i(P_{\text{real}}, P_{\text{gen}})\}_{i=1}^k$, that
  (i) is well-defined for joint distributions over (metadata, time series) pairs of the form above,
  (ii) captures both marginal statistical properties (e.g., distributions of metadata attributes, marginal value distributions of the time series, autocorrelation structure) and joint properties (e.g., dependence between metadata and temporal dynamics, and long-range temporal correlations),
  (iii) admits consistent finite-sample estimators with quantifiable error,
  (iv) does not depend on a domain-specific pretrained feature extractor.

(b) Provide criteria under which low values of the proposed metrics imply that $P_{\text{gen}}$ is suitable as a substitute for $P_{\text{real}}$ in downstream networked-systems tasks (e.g., classification, anomaly detection, simulation), and conversely identify failure modes that the metrics provably detect.

(c) Compare the proposed metrics, in terms of statistical power and computational cost, against existing alternatives such as classifier two-sample tests, predictive-score gaps (train-on-synthetic / test-on-real), and discrepancies of empirical autocorrelation or attribute distributions.
status_search_result: No universally accepted fidelity metric exists for GANs over (metadata, time series) data. Recent surveys and benchmarks (ACM Computing Surveys 2023; DeepIntoStreams evaluation pipeline; SeriesGAN 2024) note that GAN evaluation for time series still lags computer vision and relies on ad-hoc combinations of microbenchmarks (marginal/autocorrelation distances, Jensen–Shannon divergence), classifier two-sample tests (e.g., LSTM discriminator), and downstream predictive-score gaps. The problem of a principled, general fidelity metric remains open.

paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
original_question: Can GAN training for synthetic systems and networking data be combined with simulators that encode the physical constraints of the underlying system, so that data generation benefits both from statistical learning and from domain-knowledge constraints?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ denote the space of feasible trajectories of a networked system (for example, sequences of packet arrivals, throughput measurements, or system-resource time series). Suppose there is a deterministic or stochastic simulator $S:\mathcal{U}	o\mathcal{X}$ that, given control inputs $u\in\mathcal{U}$, produces outputs respecting hard physical or protocol-level constraints encoded by a constraint set $\mathcal{C}\subseteq\mathcal{X}$ (e.g., causality, conservation of bytes, queueing dynamics, link-capacity limits), so that $S(u)\in\mathcal{C}$ for all $u$. Let $\mu^*$ be an unknown distribution over $\mathcal{C}$ from which a finite sample of real networked time series is drawn.

Design a generative-adversarial framework consisting of a generator $G_	heta$, a discriminator $D_\phi$, and a coupling with the simulator $S$, together with a training objective
$$\min_	heta \max_\phi \; \mathcal{L}(G_	heta, D_\phi, S),$$
such that the induced distribution $\mu_	heta$ of generated samples satisfies the following simultaneously:

1. (Hard-constraint satisfaction) $\mathrm{supp}(\mu_	heta)\subseteq\mathcal{C}$, i.e., every generated trajectory is physically/protocol-feasible.
2. (Statistical fidelity) $\mu_	heta$ converges, in an appropriate metric (e.g., Wasserstein distance or Jensen–Shannon divergence) restricted to $\mathcal{C}$, to $\mu^*$ as the sample size and capacity grow.
3. (Strict improvement) On at least one realistic networked time-series benchmark, the framework strictly improves over both (a) a pure GAN trained without the simulator and (b) the simulator $S$ alone, with respect to a fixed downstream utility metric.

Provide such a construction together with a proof (or principled empirical demonstration) that conditions 1–3 can be met, or show that no GAN-with-simulator coupling can simultaneously achieve all three.
status_search_result: The question is a forward-looking research direction about combining GAN training with physics/protocol-aware simulators for networked time-series data generation. Subsequent work on simulator-in-the-loop and physics-informed GANs (e.g., physics-informed GANs, Sim2Real GANs, hybrid model-based generative models) has explored related ideas, but no definitive, general framework specifically resolving the combination for networked-systems data with guaranteed constraint satisfaction and statistical fidelity has been established. The problem appears to remain an open research direction.

paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
context_brief: Is differential privacy the right metric?
original_question: For networked time-series datasets in which one released sample may summarize behavior of many users or entities rather than a single person, is differential privacy an appropriate privacy metric for the data-sharing problem at all?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the problem of releasing a synthetic version of a networked time-series dataset $D = \{X^{(1)}, X^{(2)}, \ldots, X^{(n)}\}$, where each sample $X^{(i)} = (x^{(i)}_1, \ldots, x^{(i)}_T)$ is a multivariate time series (together with optional categorical metadata) that may aggregate or summarize the activity of many distinct users, devices, or entities, rather than corresponding to a single individual. Recall that a randomized mechanism $\mathcal{M}$ acting on databases is $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differentially private if for every pair of databases $D, D'$ that differ in a single record and every measurable set $S$ in the output space,
$$\Pr[\mathcal{M}(D) \in S] \le e^{\varepsilon}\, \Pr[\mathcal{M}(D') \in S] + \delta.$$
The standard "single-record" granularity of differential privacy implicitly assumes that one record corresponds to one individual whose privacy is to be protected.

Question: For networked time-series datasets of the type above, in which a single released sample $X^{(i)}$ can encode behavior of many users or entities simultaneously, formulate and decide whether differential privacy (in any of its standard variants: record-level, user-level, group, Rényi, or local DP) is an appropriate privacy metric for the data-sharing problem. Specifically, either
(a) exhibit a precise formal threat model on networked time-series data and a corresponding granularity of DP that provably captures the desired notion of "no individual entity's data is leaked," together with achievability and utility guarantees; or
(b) prove an impossibility / inadequacy result showing that no standard DP variant (with reasonable parameters and granularity) simultaneously protects all entities summarized within a single record while preserving sufficient utility for typical downstream tasks (e.g., distributional fidelity of inter-arrival times, flow sizes, or correlations across the network).
status_search_result: This is a conceptual/methodological open question about the appropriateness of differential privacy for aggregated networked time-series data. The literature on DP for time-series and network data continues to grow (e.g., user-level DP, event-level DP, pan-privacy, and recent work on DP for synthetic time-series via GANs and diffusion models), but no consensus has emerged that DP, in any standard granularity, is the "right" metric when a single record summarizes many entities. The question remains open as a research direction.

paper_title: Using GANs for Sharing Networked Time Series Data: Challenges, Initial Promise, and Open Questions
original_question: How can synthetic-data generation methods such as DoppelGANger be extended to handle networking datasets whose behavior depends on causal interactions between stateful agents rather than only on isolated per-agent traces?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a system of $N$ stateful agents indexed by $i \in \{1,\dots,N\}$, each evolving in discrete time $t = 1,\dots,T$. Each agent $i$ has a hidden state $s^{(i)}_t \in \mathcal{S}$, an observable measurement $x^{(i)}_t \in \mathcal{X}$, and an associated time-invariant attribute $a^{(i)} \in \mathcal{A}$. The agents are coupled through a (possibly time-varying) interaction graph $G_t = (V, E_t)$ on $V = \{1,\dots,N\}$, and the joint dynamics satisfy a causal update rule of the form
$$ s^{(i)}_{t+1} = f\!\left(s^{(i)}_t,\; \{x^{(j)}_t : (j,i) \in E_t\},\; a^{(i)},\; \xi^{(i)}_t\right), \qquad x^{(i)}_t = g\!\left(s^{(i)}_t,\; \eta^{(i)}_t\right), $$
for some unknown stochastic functions $f, g$ and independent noise variables $\xi^{(i)}_t, \eta^{(i)}_t$. A dataset $\mathcal{D}$ consists of i.i.d. realizations of the full collection $\bigl(\{a^{(i)}\}_i, \{x^{(i)}_t\}_{i,t}\bigr)$.

Design a generative model — extending the architecture of generative adversarial networks for mixed attribute/time-series data (in which a generator first produces per-agent attributes from noise and then unrolls a per-agent recurrent network to emit a measurement sequence, trained against a pair of discriminators on attributes and on full trajectories) — that takes $\mathcal{D}$ as training data and produces synthetic samples whose joint distribution over $\bigl(\{a^{(i)}\}_i, \{x^{(i)}_t\}_{i,t}\bigr)$ faithfully reproduces:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the marginal per-agent attribute and trajectory distributions,
\item the cross-agent dependencies induced by the latent interaction graph $\{G_t\}$, and
\item the causal temporal dependencies in which agent $i$'s behavior at time $t+1$ depends on the behaviors of its neighbors at times $\leq t$.
\end{enumerate}
Provide an explicit architecture and training objective, together with theoretical guarantees (e.g., consistency, identifiability of the interaction structure, or fidelity bounds on multi-agent statistics) under stated assumptions on $f, g$ and the graph process. In particular, determine whether such guarantees are achievable when the graph $\{G_t\}$ is unobserved and must be inferred from the data alone.
category_tag: Generative models for networked time series
status_search_result: The problem of extending DoppelGANger-style synthetic data generation to multi-agent networking datasets with causal inter-agent dependencies is described as an open challenge. Subsequent work has explored related directions (e.g., graph-based or multi-agent time-series GANs), but no published method to date provides a comprehensive, theoretically-grounded extension that handles causal interactions among stateful agents in networking traces. The problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: Answering two open problems on Banks theorem for non-autonomous dynamical systems
context_brief: Counterexample to Banks-type sensitivity without finite generation
original_question: Does there exist a non-autonomous dynamical system (X, f1,∞) on a metric space X without isolated points such that the system is topologically transitive, every point of X is periodic for the system so that Per(f1,∞) = X, and there exist two invariant periodic points x and y whose orbits are disjoint, but the system is not finitely generated and nevertheless fails to be sensitive?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space without isolated points. A non-autonomous dynamical system (NADS) on $X$ is a pair $(X, f_{1,\infty})$, where $f_{1,\infty} = (f_n)_{n\ge 1}$ is a sequence of continuous self-maps $f_n : X \to X$. For $n \ge 1$ set $f_1^n = f_n \circ f_{n-1} \circ \cdots \circ f_1$ and $f_1^0 = \mathrm{id}_X$. The orbit of a point $x \in X$ is $\mathrm{orb}(x, f_{1,\infty}) = \{f_1^n(x) : n \ge 0\}$.

Define:
\begin{itemize}
\item $(X,f_{1,\infty})$ is \emph{topologically transitive} if for every pair of nonempty open sets $U,V \subset X$ there exists $n \ge 1$ with $f_1^n(U) \cap V \neq \emptyset$.
\item A point $x \in X$ is \emph{periodic} for $f_{1,\infty}$ if there exists $k \ge 1$ with $f_1^{nk}(x) = x$ for all $n \ge 0$; let $\mathrm{Per}(f_{1,\infty})$ denote the set of such periodic points. A periodic point $x$ is \emph{invariant} if $f_n(x) = x$ for all sufficiently large (or all) $n$, equivalently the sequence $(f_1^n(x))_{n\ge 0}$ is eventually constant in a way preserved by the system.
\item $(X,f_{1,\infty})$ is \emph{sensitive (sensitive to initial conditions)} if there exists $\delta > 0$ such that for every $x \in X$ and every neighborhood $U$ of $x$, there exist $y \in U$ and $n \ge 1$ with $d(f_1^n(x), f_1^n(y)) > \delta$.
\item $(X,f_{1,\infty})$ is \emph{finitely generated} if there is a finite set $\{g_1,\dots,g_m\}$ of continuous self-maps of $X$ such that each $f_n$ belongs to $\{g_1,\dots,g_m\}$.
\end{itemize}

Question: Does there exist a non-autonomous dynamical system $(X, f_{1,\infty})$ on a metric space $X$ without isolated points such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f_{1,\infty}$ is topologically transitive,
\item $\mathrm{Per}(f_{1,\infty}) = X$,
\item there exist two invariant periodic points $x, y \in X$ with $\mathrm{orb}(x, f_{1,\infty}) \cap \mathrm{orb}(y, f_{1,\infty}) = \emptyset$,
\item $(X, f_{1,\infty})$ is \emph{not} finitely generated, and
\item $(X, f_{1,\infty})$ is \emph{not} sensitive?
\end{enumerate}
status_search_result: The question is answered affirmatively: an explicit counterexample of a non-finitely-generated NADS satisfying the transitivity, dense periodicity and disjoint invariant-orbit conditions while failing to be sensitive has been constructed, resolving the open problem in the positive direction.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: For a general infinite-dimensional control system, does every input-to-state stability Lyapunov function given in implication form also admit an equivalent dissipative-form characterization, without imposing the restrictive extra assumptions currently needed? Equivalently, is implication-form ISS Lyapunov theory fully equivalent to dissipative-form ISS Lyapunov theory in infinite dimensions, as it is for ordinary differential equations under reasonable regularity assumptions?
self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space (the state space) and $U$ a normed space of input values, and let $\mathcal{U}$ be a space of admissible input functions $u:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\to U$. Consider a control system $\Sigma$ with state trajectories $x(\cdot;x_0,u)\in X$ defined for initial state $x_0\in X$ and input $u\in\mathcal{U}$. Recall the comparison-function classes $\mathcal{K}$, $\mathcal{K}_\infty$, and $\mathcal{KL}$.

A continuous functional $V:X\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ that is locally Lipschitz on $X\setminus\{0\}$ and satisfies
$$\psi_1(\|x\|_X)\leq V(x)\leq \psi_2(\|x\|_X),\qquad \forall x\in X,$$
for some $\psi_1,\psi_2\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$, is called:

(a) an ISS Lyapunov function in dissipative form for $\Sigma$ if there exist $\alpha\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ and $\sigma\in\mathcal{K}$ such that for almost every $t\geq 0$, along every trajectory,
$$\dot V(x(t))\leq -\alpha(\|x(t)\|_X)+\sigma(\|u(t)\|_U);$$

(b) an ISS Lyapunov function in implication form for $\Sigma$ if there exist $\chi\in\mathcal{K}$ and $\alpha\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that
$$\|x\|_X\geq \chi(\|u(t)\|_U)\;\Longrightarrow\;\dot V(x(t))\leq -\alpha(\|x(t)\|_X).$$

It is straightforward that (a) implies (b). For finite-dimensional ODE systems with sufficient regularity, the converse also holds (the two notions are equivalent).

Question: Is it true, for every infinite-dimensional control system $\Sigma$ on a Banach space $X$ (in a suitable general class encompassing well-posed evolution equations), that the existence of an ISS Lyapunov function in implication form implies the existence of an ISS Lyapunov function in dissipative form, without imposing restrictive additional regularity or structural assumptions on $\Sigma$ or $V$?
status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g., a 2025 paper in Mathematics of Control, Signals, and Systems on coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular infinite-dimensional systems, and 2021–2025 works on infinite networks) continues to construct dissipative-form Lyapunov functions only under additional assumptions, treating the general equivalence in infinite dimensions as still unresolved. While equivalence has been settled for (continuous) discrete-time systems and via "strong implication form" notions, no general equivalence theorem for infinite-dimensional continuous-time systems without restrictive hypotheses appears in the located sources, so the problem appears to remain open.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: Given an infinite-dimensional system that satisfies the local input-to-state stability estimate with comparison functions β and γ, determine or estimate the actual region in the product space of states and inputs on which that LISS estimate is valid. In particular, go beyond existence proofs and obtain usable bounds for the validity region in X × U.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(X,\|\cdot\|_X)$ be a Banach space (the state space) and $(U,\|\cdot\|_U)$ a normed space of admissible input values; let $\mathcal{U}$ be a normed space of admissible input functions $u:\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\to U$ (e.g. $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0},U)$) endowed with norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{U}}$. Consider a forward complete control system $\Sigma$ on $X$ with input space $\mathcal{U}$, whose solution starting from $x\in X$ under input $u\in\mathcal{U}$ is denoted $\phi(t,x,u)$, defined for all $t\ge 0$ on the relevant domain.

Recall that a function $\gamma:\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ is of class $\mathcal{K}$ if it is continuous, strictly increasing, and $\gamma(0)=0$; it is of class $\mathcal{K}_\infty$ if additionally $\gamma(r)\to\infty$ as $r\to\infty$. A function $\beta:\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\times\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ is of class $\mathcal{KL}$ if $\beta(\cdot,t)\in\mathcal{K}$ for each fixed $t\ge 0$ and $\beta(r,t)\downarrow 0$ as $t\to\infty$ for each fixed $r\ge 0$.

The system $\Sigma$ is called locally input-to-state stable (LISS) if there exist $\beta\in\mathcal{KL}$, $\gamma\in\mathcal{K}$, and constants $\rho_x,\rho_u>0$ such that for all $x\in X$ with $\|x\|_X\le \rho_x$ and all $u\in\mathcal{U}$ with $\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}}\le \rho_u$, the trajectory $\phi(\cdot,x,u)$ exists for all $t\ge 0$ and satisfies
$$\|\phi(t,x,u)\|_X \;\le\; \beta(\|x\|_X,t) + \gamma(\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}}), \qquad t\ge 0. \tag{$\ast$}$$

More generally, given $\beta\in\mathcal{KL}$ and $\gamma\in\mathcal{K}$, define the validity region
$$R(\beta,\gamma)\;:=\;\bigl\{(x,u)\in X\times\mathcal{U} : \phi(\cdot,x,u)\text{ is global and }(\ast)\text{ holds for all }t\ge 0\bigr\}.$$

Problem. Develop a method that, beyond merely asserting the existence of some neighborhood of $(0,0)\in X\times\mathcal{U}$ contained in $R(\beta,\gamma)$, yields explicit, usable lower bounds on $R(\beta,\gamma)$ for a given LISS infinite-dimensional system $\Sigma$ and given comparison functions $\beta,\gamma$. In particular, produce constructive estimates (for instance via Lyapunov-type or other functional-analytic techniques) of the largest sublevel-style set $\{(x,u)\in X\times\mathcal{U} : \|x\|_X\le r_x,\ \|u\|_{\mathcal{U}}\le r_u\}\subset R(\beta,\gamma)$, and more generally describe quantitatively the shape of $R(\beta,\gamma)$ in $X\times\mathcal{U}$.
status_search_result: The problem of obtaining usable bounds on the validity region of a LISS estimate for infinite-dimensional systems appears to remain open. The authoritative survey on ISS for infinite-dimensional systems explicitly lists this as untouched, and recent related work (e.g., 2024–2025 papers on local integral ISS for non-autonomous infinite-dimensional systems and on estimating ISS gain functions via finite-dimensional approximations) addresses related but distinct questions, without providing general constructive estimates of the LISS validity region in $X\times\mathcal{U}$.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
context_brief: ISS versus iISS for L∞ inputs
original_question: For linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded input operators and input space L∞(R+, U), does input-to-state stability imply integral input-to-state stability? More specifically, after knowing that iISS implies ISS in this setting, determine whether the reverse implication ISS ⇒ iISS also holds for L∞ inputs.
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $X$ and $U$ be Banach spaces, and consider a linear control system
$$\dot x(t) = A x(t) + B u(t), \qquad x(0) = x_0 \in X, \qquad t \geq 0,$$
where $A : D(A) \subset X \to X$ generates a strongly continuous semigroup $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}$ on $X$ and $B \in \mathcal{L}(U, X_{-1})$ is a (possibly) unbounded admissible control operator, with $X_{-1}$ the usual extrapolation space associated with $A$. For an admissible input space $\mathcal{U} = L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$, the mild solution is
$$x(t; x_0, u) = T(t) x_0 + \int_0^t T_{-1}(t-s) B u(s)\, ds \in X.$$

Definitions.
1. The system is input-to-state stable (ISS) with respect to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$ if there exist $\beta \in \mathcal{KL}$ and $\gamma \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that for every $x_0 \in X$ and every $u \in L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$,
$$\|x(t; x_0, u)\|_X \leq \beta(\|x_0\|_X, t) + \gamma(\|u\|_{L^\infty(0,t;U)}), \qquad t \ge 0.$$
2. The system is integral input-to-state stable (iISS) with respect to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$ if there exist $\beta \in \mathcal{KL}$ and $\theta, \mu \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that for every $x_0 \in X$ and every $u \in L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$,
$$\|x(t; x_0, u)\|_X \leq \beta(\|x_0\|_X, t) + \theta\!\left(\int_0^t \mu(\|u(s)\|_U)\, ds\right), \qquad t \ge 0.$$

It is known that, in this setting, iISS with respect to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$ implies ISS with respect to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$.

Question. For linear infinite-dimensional systems of the above form with possibly unbounded admissible control operator $B$, does ISS with respect to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$ imply iISS with respect to $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}_+, U)$?
status_search_result: Recent literature on ISS for infinite-dimensional linear systems (including works on L^p–L^q ISS and Orlicz-space characterizations through 2025) treats the question of whether ISS w.r.t. L^∞ implies iISS w.r.t. L^∞ for unbounded admissible control operators as still open in general. Equivalence has been established only in special classes (e.g., parabolic diagonal systems), but no general resolution has been reported.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: Can one prove full input-to-state stability, without any restriction on input magnitude, for the Burgers equation x_t = μ x_{zz} − ν x x_z on z ∈ (0,1) with boundary conditions x(t,0)=0 and x(t,1)=u(t), when the state is measured in L2(0,1) and the input belongs to a bounded piecewise-continuous input space such as P Cb(R+, R)?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the viscous Burgers equation on the spatial interval $(0,1)$ with boundary control:
$$x_t(t,z) = \mu\, x_{zz}(t,z) - \nu\, x(t,z)\, x_z(t,z), \qquad t>0,\ z\in(0,1),$$
$$x(t,0) = 0, \qquad x(t,1) = u(t), \qquad t \ge 0,$$
with constants $\mu>0$, $\nu>0$, initial condition $x(0,\cdot)\in L^2(0,1)$, and input $u$ in the space $PC_b(\mathbb{R}_+,\mathbb{R})$ of bounded piecewise-continuous real-valued functions on $\mathbb{R}_+$, equipped with the supremum norm.

The system is called input-to-state stable (ISS) with respect to the state space $X := L^2(0,1)$ and the input space $\mathcal{U} := PC_b(\mathbb{R}_+,\mathbb{R})$ if there exist functions $\beta \in \mathcal{KL}$ and $\gamma \in \mathcal{K}$ such that for every initial state $x_0 \in L^2(0,1)$ and every input $u \in \mathcal{U}$ the corresponding (mild) solution satisfies
$$\|x(t,\cdot)\|_{L^2(0,1)} \le \beta\bigl(\|x_0\|_{L^2(0,1)},\, t\bigr) + \gamma\bigl(\|u\|_{\infty}\bigr) \qquad \text{for all } t \ge 0,$$
with no a priori restriction on the magnitude of $\|x_0\|_{L^2(0,1)}$ or $\|u\|_{\infty}$.

Question: Prove or disprove that the above boundary-controlled viscous Burgers equation is input-to-state stable in this sense, without any restriction on the magnitude of inputs (or, more generally, decide ISS for some other natural input space in place of $PC_b(\mathbb{R}_+,\mathbb{R})$).
status_search_result: The problem is posed as Open Problem 5.12 in the 2020 SIAM Review survey by Mironchenko and Prieur. Subsequent work (e.g., Zheng–Zhu) establishes ISS/iISS in $L^q$ norms for generalized Burgers-type equations with boundary disturbances under various conditions, and local/De-Giorgi-iteration based ISS results are known, but no published result establishes full (global, unrestricted-magnitude) ISS in $L^2(0,1)$ with $PC_b$ boundary inputs for the standard viscous Burgers equation. The status appears to remain open.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: Clarify the relationships between the various small-gain conditions used for infinite networks of interconnected systems, such as spectral small-gain conditions, robust strong small-gain conditions, existence of Ω-paths, and monotone invertibility of id − Γ. Use that understanding to derive input-to-state stability small-gain theorems for infinite networks with nonlinear gains.
self_contained_problem:
Consider an infinite network of interconnected control systems indexed by a countable set $I$. Each subsystem $\Sigma_i$ has state $x_i$ in some Banach space, an external input $u_i$, and is interconnected with the other subsystems through nonlinear gains $\gamma_{ij}\in\mathcal{K}_\infty\cup\{0\}$ that quantify the influence of $x_j$ on $x_i$. Assume each $\Sigma_i$ is input-to-state stable (ISS) with respect to its inputs and to the states of its neighbors, with gains $\gamma_{ij}$.

Form the (in general infinite-dimensional) nonlinear monotone gain operator
$$\Gamma:\ell_+^\infty(I)	o \ell_+^\infty(I),\qquad \Gamma(s)_i=\sup_{j\in I}\gamma_{ij}(s_j),$$
and consider the following candidate small-gain conditions on $\Gamma$:

(a) Spectral small-gain condition: $r(\Gamma)<1$ in an appropriate spectral-radius sense for monotone (sub-)linear maps.

(b) Robust strong small-gain condition: there exists $ho\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that $D_ho\circ\Gamma$ has a suitable global stability property, where $D_ho(s)=((\mathrm{id}+ho)(s_i))_i$.

(c) Existence of an $\Omega$-path: a continuous, componentwise strictly increasing path $\sigma:[0,\infty)	o\ell_+^\infty(I)$ with $\sigma(0)=0$, $\sigma(r)	o\infty$ as $r	o\infty$, such that $\Gamma(\sigma(r))<\sigma(r)$ componentwise for all $r>0$.

(d) Monotone invertibility of $\mathrm{id}-\Gamma$: for every $w\in\ell_+^\infty(I)$, the inequality $v\le \Gamma(v)+w$ implies $v\le\chi(\|w\|)\mathbf{1}$ for some $\chi\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ (equivalently a monotone bounded invertibility property of $\mathrm{id}-\Gamma$).

Problem. (i) Determine the precise logical relationships (implications, equivalences, and counterexamples) among conditions (a)–(d) for infinite networks (it is known that for finite networks under standard assumptions they are essentially equivalent). (ii) Using these relationships, formulate and prove ISS small-gain theorems for infinite networks of interconnected ISS systems with general nonlinear gains $\gamma_{ij}$, giving conditions on $\Gamma$ that guarantee ISS of the whole interconnection (in trajectory and/or Lyapunov form).
status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the question was posed. Kawan, Mironchenko, Noroozi, Schwenninger, Zamani and collaborators (e.g., "Nonlinear small-gain theorems for ISS of infinite interconnections", MCSS 2021/2022; "A Lyapunov-based ISS small-gain theorem for infinite networks of nonlinear systems", arXiv:2103.07439; "ISS small-gain criteria for infinite networks with linear gains", 2021; and "The small-gain condition for infinite networks modeled on $\ell^\infty$-spaces", arXiv:2503.03925) have clarified key relationships: the monotone limit property, uniform small-gain condition, and monotone bounded invertibility of $\mathrm{id}-\Gamma$ are equivalent in broad settings, and existence of a path of strict decay (Ω-path) yields trajectory- and Lyapunov-based ISS small-gain theorems for countable networks. However, the full picture (including the spectral small-gain condition and general nonlinear gains over arbitrary state spaces) is not yet completely settled, so the problem is partially solved.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: For retarded time-delay systems, is it sufficient to require a pointwise dissipation inequality of the form |x(0)| ≥ χ(‖u‖_U) ⇒ V̇_u(x) ≤ −α(|x(0)|) in order to conclude ISS? Equivalently, can the stronger Lyapunov-Krasovskii hypothesis V(x) ≥ χ(|u(0)|) ⇒ V̇_u(x) ≤ −α(|x(0)|) be weakened to a condition that depends only on the current state magnitude and full input norm?
self_contained_problem:
Consider a retarded nonlinear time-delay system of the form
    ẋ(t) = f(x_t, u(t)),    t ≥ 0,
where, for some maximum delay r > 0, the state history is x_t ∈ C([−r,0]; ℝ^n) defined by x_t(θ) = x(t+θ), the input u: [0,∞) → U takes values in a normed input space (U, |·|_U) and is locally essentially bounded, and f: C([−r,0]; ℝ^n) × U → ℝ^n is locally Lipschitz and ensures forward completeness of solutions. The system is called input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K_∞ such that
    |x(t)| ≤ β(‖x_0‖_C, t) + γ(‖u‖_{L^∞(0,t;U)})
for every initial condition x_0 ∈ C([−r,0]; ℝ^n), every admissible input u, and every t ≥ 0.

Let V: C([−r,0]; ℝ^n) → ℝ_{≥0} be a continuous Lyapunov–Krasovskii functional that is locally Lipschitz on bounded sets, and assume there exist ψ_1, ψ_2 ∈ K_∞ with
    ψ_1(|φ(0)|) ≤ V(φ) ≤ ψ_2(‖φ‖_C)    for all φ ∈ C([−r,0]; ℝ^n).
For an absolutely continuous solution x(·) corresponding to input u, denote by V̇_u(x_t) the upper-right Dini derivative of t ↦ V(x_t) along trajectories.

Question. Do there exist α, χ ∈ K_∞ such that the pointwise dissipation implication
    |x(0)| ≥ χ(‖u‖_U)    ⟹    V̇_u(x_t) ≤ −α(|x(0)|)
(where |x(0)| denotes the magnitude of the current state value x_t(0) and ‖u‖_U denotes the essential supremum norm of the input) is by itself sufficient to imply that the system is ISS? Equivalently, can the standard Lyapunov–Krasovskii sufficient condition
    V(x_t) ≥ χ(|u(t)|)    ⟹    V̇_u(x_t) ≤ −α(|x(0)|)
be weakened to the above condition, which depends only on the current state magnitude and the full input norm?
status_search_result: The question is generally regarded as still open in full generality. Partial results exist: the analogous statement for integral ISS (iISS) has been answered positively, and recent work shows that if the Lyapunov–Krasovskii functional with pointwise dissipation also yields uniform global stability, then ISS follows. A 2026 superposition-based approach gives further partial progress, but no complete proof or counterexample for the full conjecture has been published.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: Achieve a full understanding of the relationship between input-to-state stability and integral input-to-state stability for linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded input operators. This asks for a general structural picture, not just isolated positive or negative examples.
self_contained_problem:
Consider linear control systems of the form
  ẋ(t) = Ax(t) + Bu(t),  x(0) = x₀ ∈ X,
where X is a Banach (or Hilbert) space, A : D(A) ⊂ X → X generates a strongly continuous semigroup (T(t))_{t≥0} on X, and B ∈ L(U, X_{-1}) is a (possibly unbounded) admissible input operator with U a Banach space and X_{-1} the extrapolation space associated with A. Inputs u are taken from L^∞_loc([0,∞); U).

Such a system is called input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K_∞ such that, for every x₀ ∈ X and every admissible input u,
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x₀‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_{L^∞(0,t;U)})  for all t ≥ 0.

It is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and θ, μ ∈ K_∞ such that
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x₀‖_X, t) + θ(∫₀^t μ(‖u(s)‖_U) ds)  for all t ≥ 0.

Provide a complete structural characterization of the relationship between ISS and iISS for this class of linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded admissible input operators B. Specifically, determine necessary and sufficient conditions, expressed in terms of (A, B, X, U), under which ISS implies iISS, under which iISS implies ISS, and identify the precise gap between the two notions in this setting (going beyond isolated examples and counterexamples to a general theory).
category_tag: Input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional linear systems
status_search_result: A 2025 preprint develops integral-to-integral ISS admissibility theory for linear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded input operators, advancing the topic. While the bounded-B case is well understood (ISS and iISS coincide via exponential stability), a general structural characterization for unbounded admissible B remains incomplete; recent literature explicitly notes the question is much harder and several notorious sub-questions persist.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: Develop a theory of non-coercive integral input-to-state Lyapunov functions for infinite-dimensional systems, including their basic properties and their usefulness for proving iISS. At present this non-coercive iISS Lyapunov theory has not been investigated.
self_contained_problem:
Consider an abstract control system $\Sigma = (X, \mathcal{U}, \phi)$ where $(X, \|\cdot\|_X)$ is a Banach space (the state space), $\mathcal{U}$ is a normed vector space of admissible input functions $u : \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} \to U$ with values in a normed space $U$, and $\phi : D_\phi \subset \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} \times X \times \mathcal{U} \to X$ is a transition map satisfying the usual axioms (identity, causality, cocycle property, continuity).

Recall the standard comparison-function classes: $\mathcal{K}$, $\mathcal{K}_\infty$, $\mathcal{L}$, and $\mathcal{KL}$.

The system $\Sigma$ is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist $\beta \in \mathcal{KL}$ and $\alpha, \gamma \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that for all $x \in X$, all admissible $u \in \mathcal{U}$, and all $t \geq 0$,
$$\alpha(\|\phi(t,x,u)\|_X) \leq \beta(\|x\|_X, t) + \int_0^t \gamma(\|u(s)\|_U)\, ds.$$

A continuous function $V : X \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ with $V(0)=0$ is called a coercive iISS Lyapunov function if there exist $\psi_1, \psi_2 \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$, $\alpha \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$ (or positive definite), and $\sigma \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that
$$\psi_1(\|x\|_X) \leq V(x) \leq \psi_2(\|x\|_X), \qquad \dot V_u(x) \leq -\alpha(\|x\|_X) + \sigma(\|u\|_U),$$
where $\dot V_u$ denotes an appropriate (Dini or Lie) derivative of $V$ along trajectories. Dropping the lower bound $\psi_1(\|x\|_X) \leq V(x)$ (so only $0 \leq V(x) \leq \psi_2(\|x\|_X)$ is required) yields a non-coercive iISS Lyapunov function candidate.

Develop a theory of non-coercive integral input-to-state Lyapunov functions for infinite-dimensional systems of the above type. Specifically:

(a) Identify the appropriate definition (or definitions) of a non-coercive iISS Lyapunov function for $\Sigma$.

(b) Establish their basic properties (existence, regularity, behaviour along trajectories, relations to coercive iISS Lyapunov functions, and converse-Lyapunov style results).

(c) Prove sufficient conditions under which the existence of a non-coercive iISS Lyapunov function implies that $\Sigma$ is iISS, and identify minimal additional regularity hypotheses (e.g., on the semigroup, well-posedness, or admissibility of the input operator) needed for such an implication.
status_search_result: Non-coercive Lyapunov function theory for infinite-dimensional systems has been substantially developed since 2019 (Mironchenko–Wirth, JDE 2019; SIAM J. Control Optim. 2020), extending to ISS and to certain iISS/LISS settings via norm-to-integral ISS characterizations and constructions for time-varying semilinear evolution equations. However, a fully developed theory of non-coercive iISS Lyapunov functions with general converse results matching the coercive case does not yet appear in the literature; recent works (e.g., 2025 papers on coercive ISS-Lyapunov functionals for regular systems and 2025 time-varying evolution equation results) treat related but partial settings. The problem is therefore best classified as partially solved.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: Build an integral input-to-state stability theory for bilinear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded bilinear operators. The paper identifies this part of the theory as still being in its infancy.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a bilinear control system on a Banach space $X$ of the form
$$\dot x(t) = A x(t) + B(u(t), x(t)), \qquad x(0) = x_0 \in X,$$
where $A : D(A) \subset X \to X$ is the generator of a strongly continuous semigroup $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}$ on $X$, $u \in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}([0,\infty); U)$ is an input from a Banach space $U$, and $B : U \times X \to X_{-1}$ is a continuous bilinear map taking values in the extrapolation space $X_{-1}$ associated with $A$ (so that $B$ is, in general, an unbounded bilinear operator with respect to the state space $X$). Mild solutions are defined in $X_{-1}$ and assumed to belong to $X$ for all $t\ge 0$.

The system is called integral input-to-state stable (iISS) if there exist $\beta \in \mathcal{KL}$ and $\theta, \mu \in \mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that for every $x_0 \in X$ and every admissible input $u$,
$$\|x(t)\|_X \le \beta(\|x_0\|_X, t) + \theta\!\left(\int_0^t \mu(\|u(s)\|_U)\, ds\right), \qquad t \ge 0.$$

Develop a systematic integral input-to-state stability theory for such bilinear infinite-dimensional systems with unbounded bilinear operators $B$. In particular:

(a) Provide verifiable sufficient conditions on $A$, $B$, $X$, and $U$ ensuring that the system is iISS.
(b) Characterize iISS in terms of qualitative properties such as 0-uniform global asymptotic stability and suitable Lyapunov-type functions adapted to the unbounded setting.
(c) Identify a class of admissible inputs (e.g., subspaces of $L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}$ guaranteeing well-posedness) for which the theory is consistent, and apply the resulting criteria to representative PDE examples with boundary or otherwise unbounded bilinear control.
status_search_result: Significant progress has been made: Hosfeld, Jacob, and Schwenninger (Math. Control Signals Systems, 2022; arXiv:1811.08470) established iISS results for unbounded bilinear control systems on Hilbert spaces, including sufficient conditions and applications such as a bilinearly controlled Fokker–Planck equation. Subsequent work has extended ISS/iISS estimates to bilinear feedback systems with applications to viscous Burgers, Schrödinger, Navier–Stokes, and semilinear wave equations. However, a fully general theory covering arbitrary unbounded bilinear operators on Banach spaces is not yet complete, so the program is partially solved.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: Develop an input-to-output stability theory for infinite-dimensional systems with outputs, analogous to the mature finite-dimensional IOS theory. This includes general criteria, Lyapunov tools, and structural results for systems where the quantity of interest is an output h(x,u) rather than the full state.
self_contained_problem:
Consider a control system $\Sigma=(X,\mathcal{U},\phi)$ where $X$ is a Banach space (the state space), $\mathcal{U}$ is a normed space of admissible input functions $u:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\to U$ (with $U$ a normed input-value space), and $\phi:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\times X\times\mathcal{U}\to X$ is a transition map satisfying the standard axioms of a forward-complete control system (identity, causality, cocycle property, continuity in initial state). Equip the system with an output map $h:X\times U\to Y$ taking values in a Banach output space $Y$; write $H(t,x,u):=h(\phi(t,x,u),u(t))$.

Recall the standard comparison-function classes: $\mathcal{K}$, $\mathcal{K}_\infty$, $\mathcal{L}$, and $\mathcal{KL}$. The system $(\Sigma,h)$ is called input-to-output stable (IOS) if there exist $\beta\in\mathcal{KL}$ and $\gamma\in\mathcal{K}_\infty$ such that for every $x\in X$, every $u\in\mathcal{U}$, and every $t\geq 0$,
$$\|H(t,x,u)\|_Y \;\leq\; \beta(\|x\|_X,t) + \gamma(\|u\|_{\mathcal{U}}).$$

Develop a theory of input-to-output stability for such infinite-dimensional systems with outputs that parallels the finite-dimensional IOS theory. In particular, address the following:

1. (Superposition / characterization theorem.) Identify weaker stability-like properties (analogues of output asymptotic gain, output Lagrange stability, output limit property, output continuity at the equilibrium, etc.) whose conjunction is equivalent to IOS, and determine which combinations are sufficient versus insufficient in the infinite-dimensional setting.

2. (Lyapunov characterizations.) Define an appropriate notion of IOS Lyapunov function $V:X\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ involving the output norm $\|h(x,u)\|_Y$, and prove that the existence of such a function is equivalent (or, where this fails, obtain the strongest possible implications) to IOS.

3. (Structural / small-gain results.) Establish small-gain theorems for feedback interconnections and (possibly infinite) networks of IOS subsystems on Banach spaces, giving verifiable conditions on the gain operators that guarantee IOS of the interconnection.

Provide the criteria, Lyapunov tools, and structural results, and identify intrinsic obstructions specific to the infinite-dimensional case (e.g., examples showing classical finite-dimensional equivalences fail).
status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., a 2024 preprint titled "Characterization of input-to-output stability for infinite-dimensional systems", arXiv:2410.06013) provides superposition-type characterizations of IOS for broad classes of infinite-dimensional continuous- and discrete-time systems with outputs, in terms of weaker properties (OUAG, OULS, OCEP, etc.), and shows that some finite-dimensional characterizations cannot be extended verbatim. Small-gain results for IOS networks of infinite-dimensional systems have also appeared. However, a full theory paralleling the finite-dimensional case—including complete Lyapunov characterizations and a comprehensive structural framework—is still under development, so the program is only partially solved.

paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
original_question: Turn ISS theory into systematic robust controller-design methodology for infinite-dimensional systems and PDEs. More concretely, develop practical ISS-based design methods for boundary or distributed robust controllers across important application areas where robust control design remains largely open.
self_contained_problem:
Develop a systematic robust controller-design methodology for infinite-dimensional control systems—particularly those governed by partial differential equations (PDEs)—based on the framework of input-to-state stability (ISS).

Setup and definitions. Consider a control system of the form
  ẋ(t) = A x(t) + f(x(t), u(t), d(t)),  x(0) = x₀ ∈ X,
where X is a Banach (or Hilbert) state space, A generates a strongly continuous semigroup on X (or, more generally, the dynamics are described by an evolution equation on X possibly with unbounded boundary input operators), u(·) takes values in a control space U, and d(·) ∈ L^∞(ℝ₊; D) represents an exogenous disturbance taking values in a normed space D. Boundary control is allowed: inputs may enter through boundary conditions of the underlying PDE.

The closed-loop system under a feedback law u = K(x) is said to be input-to-state stable (ISS) with respect to the disturbance d if there exist a class-KL function β and a class-K function γ such that, for every x₀ ∈ X and every admissible d,
  ‖x(t)‖_X ≤ β(‖x₀‖_X, t) + γ(‖d‖_{L^∞(0,t;D)})  for all t ≥ 0.

Problem. Provide a constructive design framework that, given a class of PDE control systems (for example, parabolic or hyperbolic PDEs in one or several space dimensions, with either distributed or boundary actuation), produces feedback laws K—possibly together with ISS-Lyapunov functionals certifying the closed-loop ISS estimate above—and that is general enough to address concrete robust control problems in which a systematic methodology is currently lacking, such as:
  (a) the drilling problem (axial/torsional vibrations modeled by wave equations with nonlinear boundary conditions);
  (b) robust stabilization of flexible aircraft structures (beam/plate equations coupled with rigid-body dynamics and uncertain aerodynamic loads).

The methodology should specify (i) the admissible classes of disturbances and uncertainties, (ii) the construction of ISS-Lyapunov functionals for the closed loop, (iii) verifiable sufficient conditions on the controller gains ensuring the desired ISS gain γ, and (iv) extensions to cases with unbounded input operators arising from boundary actuation.
category_tag: Input-to-state stability and robust control of PDEs
status_search_result: The development of a systematic ISS-based robust controller-design methodology for infinite-dimensional and PDE systems is recognized as a broad open research direction. While Lyapunov-based ISS analysis and small-gain results have advanced (e.g., for ODE-PDE interconnections and networks of infinite-dimensional systems), no comprehensive constructive design framework covering the cited application areas (drilling, flexible aircraft structures) has been established. Recent surveys and tutorials (2020–2021) continue to list robust ISS-based design as an active and largely open problem.
