original_question: Is it true that a non-spreading homeomorphism of the 2-torus has conjugates arbitrarily close to a rotation ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T}^2 = \mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}^2$ be the 2-torus, and let $\mathrm{Homeo}_0(\mathbb{T}^2)$ denote the group of homeomorphisms of $\mathbb{T}^2$ that are isotopic to the identity, endowed with the uniform (compact-open) topology. A homeomorphism $f \in \mathrm{Homeo}_0(\mathbb{T}^2)$ is said to be non-spreading if for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $\delta > 0$ such that, for every $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ and every set $E \subset \mathbb{T}^2$ of diameter at most $\delta$ (measured with respect to a fixed Riemannian distance), the iterate $f^n(E)$ has diameter at most $\varepsilon$.

A rotation of $\mathbb{T}^2$ is a map of the form $R_\alpha(x) = x + \alpha \pmod{\mathbb{Z}^2}$ for some $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}^2$.

Question: Is it true that for every non-spreading homeomorphism $f$ of $\mathbb{T}^2$, the closure of the conjugacy class
$$\{ h \circ f \circ h^{-1} : h \in \mathrm{Homeo}_0(\mathbb{T}^2) \}$$
in $\mathrm{Homeo}_0(\mathbb{T}^2)$ contains a rotation? Equivalently, can $f$ be conjugated to maps arbitrarily close to some rotation $R_\alpha$ in the uniform topology?
status_search_result: The question appears in a recent problem list (2025) on foliations and diffeomorphism groups and is stated as an open question. For the 2-torus the analogous statement (with rotations replacing the identity) remains an open conjecture, supported by partial results in pseudo-rotation theory.

self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)_0$ denote the identity component of the group of real analytic diffeomorphisms of a closed real analytic manifold $M$, equipped with its natural topology. A body of results is known concerning real analytic group actions on manifolds, including perfectness/simplicity results for $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(M)_0$ for certain manifolds $M$ (for example $S^1$ and various low-dimensional manifolds admitting suitable circle actions), and rigidity/structure theorems for real analytic actions of finitely generated groups, governing the structure of orbits, exceptional minimal sets, and associated cohomological invariants.

A codimension one real analytic foliation $\mathcal F$ on a closed real analytic manifold $M$ is a partition of $M$ into immersed real analytic hypersurfaces (leaves) given locally as the level sets of a submersion to $\mathbb R$, with transition data being real analytic. The holonomy pseudogroup of $\mathcal F$ is a pseudogroup of local real analytic diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb R$ (or of a 1-manifold transverse to the foliation).

Problem. Develop, for codimension one real analytic foliations $\mathcal F$ on closed real analytic manifolds, an analogue of the structure theory available for real analytic group actions. In particular, do the known structural and rigidity results for real analytic group actions (perfectness/simplicity of identity components of analytic diffeomorphism groups; classification of minimal sets; constraints on holonomy and on associated cohomological invariants such as powers of the Euler class) admit natural generalizations in which the role of the group action is played by the holonomy pseudogroup of $\mathcal F$?
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a 2024 problem list on foliations and diffeomorphism groups. Web search did not surface any subsequent work claiming to have generalized the analytic group-action theory (e.g., perfectness of Diff^ω_0 and rigidity of analytic actions) to codimension one real analytic foliations. The status thus appears to remain open.

original_question: Can we show that G is dense in Diff ω (S1 )0 ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R}) = \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\{\pm I\}$ act on the circle $S^1$ by Möbius transformations, and set $G_1 := \mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$, viewed as a topological group of real-analytic diffeomorphisms of $S^1$. For each integer $n \geq 1$, let $p_n \colon G_n \to G_1$ denote the $n$-fold cyclic connected covering of $G_1$; the group $G_n$ acts on $S^1$ as a group of real-analytic diffeomorphisms by lifting the action of $G_1$ through the $n$-fold cover $S^1 \to S^1$. Let $R_1 \subset G_1$ be the rotation subgroup (isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$) and set $R_n := p_n^{-1}(R_1)$, which is again isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$. For each $n \geq 1$ define
$$ G^{(n)} := G_1 \ast_{R_1} G_2 \ast_{R_2} \cdots \ast_{R_{n-1}} G_n,$$
the iterated amalgamated free product of $G_1, \ldots, G_n$ along the common rotation subgroup, realized as a subgroup of $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(S^1)_0$ (the identity component of the group of orientation-preserving real-analytic diffeomorphisms of $S^1$). The natural inclusions $G^{(n)} \hookrightarrow G^{(n+1)}$ form a direct system, and we set
$$ G := \varinjlim_{n} G^{(n)} \;\subseteq\; \mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(S^1)_0.$$
Equip $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(S^1)_0$ with its standard topology (uniform convergence of all derivatives on $S^1$, or equivalently the inductive-limit topology coming from real-analytic extensions to annular neighborhoods of $S^1$).

Question: Is $G$ dense in $\mathrm{Diff}^{\omega}(S^1)_0$?
status_search_result: The question is attributed to Tsuboi and, as noted shortly after it was posed, was resolved by work of James Giblin and Vladimir Markovic on closed transitive subgroups of $\mathrm{Homeo}(S^1)$, which classifies such subgroups and implies the asserted density. Thus the question is regarded as solved in the affirmative.

original_question: Is B Γ̄q 2q-connected i.e. do πi (B Γ̄q ) vanish for all i ≤ 2q?
self_contained_problem:
Let $q$ be a positive integer. A codimension-$q$ Haefliger structure on a topological space $X$ is, informally, a maximal atlas of local submersions to $\mathbb{R}^q$ together with germs of holonomy transition diffeomorphisms. The (smooth) Haefliger groupoid $\Gamma_q$ is the topological groupoid whose objects form $\mathbb{R}^q$ and whose morphisms are germs of locally defined $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^q$, with the sheaf (germ) topology. Its classifying space $B\Gamma_q$ classifies codimension-$q$ Haefliger structures up to concordance.

There is a natural map $
u : B\Gamma_q 	o BO(q)$ classifying the normal bundle of a Haefliger structure. Let $B\overline{\Gamma}_q$ denote the homotopy fiber of $
u$; equivalently, $B\overline{\Gamma}_q$ is the classifying space of codimension-$q$ Haefliger structures equipped with a trivialization of the normal bundle (framed Haefliger structures).

It is a classical theorem that $B\overline{\Gamma}_q$ is $q$-connected, and (Mather–Thurston / Tsuboi type results) that $B\overline{\Gamma}_q$ is in fact $(2q-1)$-connected when smooth structures of class $C^\infty$ are used, for the strongest currently known degree of connectivity in some settings.

Problem. Determine whether $B\overline{\Gamma}_q$ is $2q$-connected; that is, decide whether
$$\pi_i(B\overline{\Gamma}_q) = 0 \quad 	ext{for all } i \le 2q.$$
status_search_result: This is the long-standing Haefliger–Thurston conjecture on the connectivity of the classifying space of framed codimension-$q$ Haefliger structures. It remains open in general; partial progress (e.g., proofs of $(2q-1)$-connectivity, and results in special cases or under PL/topological hypotheses) has been made, but $2q$-connectivity has not been established.

original_question: Let Γq be the groupoid of the germs of local diffeomorphisms of Rq , and Gq ⊂ Γq be the subgroup fixing 0. Let B Ḡq be the homotopy-theoretic fibre of the map BGq → BGLq (R) classifying the normal bundle of the universal Gq -structure. Is B Ḡq homotopically trivial in B Γ̄q ?
self_contained_problem:
Let $q\geq 1$. Let $\Gamma_q$ denote the (topological) groupoid of germs of local $C^\infty$-diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^q$, and let $G_q\subset\Gamma_q$ be the subgroupoid consisting of germs fixing the origin $0\in\mathbb{R}^q$. Let $B\Gamma_q$ and $BG_q$ denote their classifying spaces (Haefliger classifying spaces). Taking the derivative at $0$ gives a map $BG_q\to BGL_q(\mathbb{R})$ which classifies the normal bundle of the universal $G_q$-structure; let $B\bar G_q$ be the homotopy fibre of this map. Similarly let $B\bar\Gamma_q$ be the homotopy fibre of $B\Gamma_q\to BGL_q(\mathbb{R})$. The inclusion $G_q\hookrightarrow\Gamma_q$ induces a map $B\bar G_q\to B\bar\Gamma_q$.

Question: Is the map $B\bar G_q\to B\bar\Gamma_q$ null-homotopic? Equivalently, is $B\bar G_q$ homotopically trivial inside $B\bar\Gamma_q$?
status_search_result: The question, originally posed by Tsuboi (1984) under the heading "foliations with only one leaf," concerns the homotopy triviality of the classifying space of the germ-stabilizer subgroupoid inside the framed Haefliger classifying space. Web searches surface Tsuboi's and Hurder's surveys on classifying spaces for foliations but reveal no resolution; the problem continues to be cited as an open question in recent foliation-theory problem lists.

original_question: Is the space BΓn is n + 1-connected?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma_n$ denote the Haefliger groupoid of germs of local $C^\infty$-diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $B\Gamma_n$ be its classifying space (which classifies codimension-$n$ Haefliger structures on topological spaces). It is a classical theorem of Haefliger (and refined by Mather–Thurston) that $B\Gamma_n$ is $n$-connected, i.e. $\pi_i(B\Gamma_n)=0$ for $1\le i\le n$.

Determine whether $B\Gamma_n$ is $(n+1)$-connected; equivalently, decide whether $\pi_{n+1}(B\Gamma_n) = 0$ for every integer $n\ge 1$.
status_search_result: This is the Haefliger conjecture (sometimes called the Haefliger–Thurston conjecture) on the connectivity of $B\Gamma_n$ in the smooth ($C^\infty$) setting. In the $C^r$ category with $r\ne n,n+1$, related connectivity results are known, and Meigniez (arXiv:2103.13897, 2021) announced a proof for framed Haefliger structures of codimension $q$ showing $(2q-1)$-connectivity. The full smooth Haefliger conjecture asserting $(n+1)$-connectivity of $B\Gamma_n$ for all $n$ is generally regarded as still open.

original_question: Are these two kerGV ’s trivial or not?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\overline{\Gamma}_1^{r}$ denote Haefliger's groupoid of germs of orientation-preserving local $C^{r}$-diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb{R}$ (with the topology that trivialises the normal bundle), for $r=\infty$ (smooth) and $r=\omega$ (real analytic). Let $B\overline{\Gamma}_1^{r}$ be its classifying space. The Godbillon–Vey class defines a homomorphism
$$
\mathrm{GV}\colon H_{3}\bigl(B\overline{\Gamma}_1^{r};\mathbb{Z}\bigr)\longrightarrow \mathbb{R},
$$
whose kernel we denote by $\ker\mathrm{GV}^{r}\subset H_{3}(B\overline{\Gamma}_1^{r};\mathbb{Z})$.

Determine whether the kernels $\ker\mathrm{GV}^{\infty}$ and $\ker\mathrm{GV}^{\omega}$ are trivial. Equivalently, decide, for each of $r\in\{\infty,\omega\}$, whether every codimension-one Haefliger $C^{r}$-structure of class in $H_{3}(B\overline{\Gamma}_1^{r};\mathbb{Z})$ with vanishing Godbillon–Vey invariant is itself null-homologous.
status_search_result: The question appears in a 2025 problem list compiled from the CIRM 2024 conference on Foliations and Diffeomorphism Groups, where it is posed as an open question. No subsequent literature was found resolving the triviality of the kernel of the Godbillon–Vey homomorphism on $H_3(B\overline{\Gamma}_1^{\infty})$ or $H_3(B\overline{\Gamma}_1^{\omega})$; both remain longstanding open problems in foliation theory.

paper_title: Open problems UP24
context_brief: Riesz equilibrium support for d−3 < s < d
original_question: For the Riesz s-energy with radial external field V(x)=γ‖x‖^α/α on R^d, what can be said about the equilibrium measure μ_eq when d−3 < s < d? In particular, in this range, when does the minimizing equilibrium support remain a sphere, and when can it instead be a full ball or another type of set?
self_contained_problem:
Fix integers d ≥ 2 and a real parameter s with 0 < s < d. For x ∈ R^d, write ‖x‖ for the Euclidean norm, and define the Riesz s-kernel k_s(x,y) = ‖x − y‖^{−s} (interpreted as −log‖x − y‖ in the limiting case s = 0). Given an external field V : R^d → R, the weighted Riesz s-energy of a Borel probability measure μ on R^d is

   I_{s,V}(μ) = ∫∫ k_s(x,y) dμ(x) dμ(y) + 2 ∫ V(x) dμ(x).

Take the radial external field V(x) = γ ‖x‖^α / α with γ > 0 and α > max(0, −s), so that I_{s,V} admits a unique minimizer μ_eq among Borel probability measures on R^d (the equilibrium measure).

Question. For parameters s in the range d − 3 < s < d, characterize the equilibrium measure μ_eq of the functional I_{s,V}. In particular, determine for which combinations of (d, s, α, γ) the support of μ_eq is a sphere {x : ‖x‖ = R} (with μ_eq the uniform/rotation-invariant probability measure on it), for which combinations the support is a full ball {x : ‖x‖ ≤ R}, and what other support geometries can arise. Provide explicit conditions distinguishing these regimes and, where possible, an explicit formula for μ_eq.
status_search_result: Recent work (2024–2025) by Chafaï, Saff, Womersley and collaborators gives a complete characterization of when the equilibrium support is a sphere for power-type radial external fields, and resolves the special case s = d − 3 (extending Marcel Riesz's classical ball result), where μ_eq is an arcsine-type radial distribution on a ball. However, a full description of μ_eq throughout the entire hypersingular-adjacent range d − 3 < s < d (including all transitions between sphere, ball and intermediate supports) is not yet complete, so the question is partially solved.

paper_title: Open problems UP24
original_question: For the Riesz s-energy with radial external field V(x)=γ‖x‖^α/α, what is the structure of the equilibrium measure μ_eq in the regime max{−s,0} < α < α_{s,d}, where α_{s,d} is the sharp threshold above which the equilibrium support is a sphere? For example, can the minimizer split into several components such as multiple spheres together with isolated points?
self_contained_problem:
Fix integers $d\ge 2$ and a parameter $s$ with $-2<s<d$ (with $s\ne 0$; the value $s=0$ corresponds to the logarithmic kernel). For $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^d$ define the Riesz $s$-kernel
$$k_s(x,y)=\begin{cases}\|x-y\|^{-s},&s\ne 0,\\ -\log\|x-y\|,&s=0,\end{cases}$$
and, for parameters $\gamma>0$ and $\alpha>\max\{-s,0\}$, define the radial external field
$$V(x)=\frac{\gamma}{\alpha}\,\|x\|^{\alpha},\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^d.$$
For a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ consider the weighted Riesz energy
$$\mathcal{E}_{s,V}(\mu)=\iint k_s(x,y)\,d\mu(x)\,d\mu(y)+2\int V(x)\,d\mu(x).$$
Under the stated assumptions there exists a unique compactly supported probability measure $\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}=\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}(s,d,\alpha,\gamma)$ minimizing $\mathcal{E}_{s,V}$ over all Borel probability measures of finite energy.

It is known that there is a sharp threshold $\alpha_{s,d}>\max\{-s,0\}$ such that for every $\alpha\ge \alpha_{s,d}$ the support of $\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is a sphere centered at the origin (with explicit uniform density on that sphere), while for $\alpha<\alpha_{s,d}$ this is not the case.

Determine the structure of $\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}$ in the sub-threshold regime
$$\max\{-s,0\}<\alpha<\alpha_{s,d}.$$
In particular, characterize the support of $\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}$: can it consist of several disjoint components, e.g.\ a union of finitely many concentric spheres, possibly together with isolated points or lower-dimensional pieces, and in each case give the corresponding density of $\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}$.
status_search_result: The sharp threshold $\alpha_{s,d}$ above which the equilibrium support is a sphere was characterized in work by Chafaï, Matzke, Saff and collaborators ("Riesz Energy with a Radial External Field: When is the Equilibrium Support a Sphere?", Potential Analysis 63 (2025), 705–738; arXiv:2405.00120). The structure of the equilibrium measure in the sub-threshold regime $\max\{-s,0\}<\alpha<\alpha_{s,d}$ is explicitly posed there as an open question (attributed to Womersley and Saff), and we found no publication resolving it.

paper_title: Open problems UP24
original_question: In deriving lower bounds and asymptotic information for minimal logarithmic and Riesz energies on the sphere, are there resummation methods more efficient than the summation-by-parts and inner-product-expansion approach described here?
self_contained_problem:
For an integer $d\geq 2$, let $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:|x|=1\}$ denote the unit sphere with its normalized surface measure. For $N\geq 2$ and a parameter $s$, define the discrete Riesz $s$-energy of an $N$-point configuration $\omega_N=\{x_1,\dots,x_N\}\subset\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$ by
$$E_s(\omega_N)=\sum_{i\neq j}\frac{1}{|x_i-x_j|^s}\quad (s>0),\qquad E_{\log}(\omega_N)=\sum_{i\neq j}\log\frac{1}{|x_i-x_j|}\quad (s=0),$$
and let $\mathcal{E}_s(N)=\min_{\omega_N}E_s(\omega_N)$ (and analogously $\mathcal{E}_{\log}(N)$) be the corresponding minimal energy.

A standard route to lower bounds and asymptotic expansions of $\mathcal{E}_s(N)$ and $\mathcal{E}_{\log}(N)$ as $N\to\infty$ proceeds by expanding the kernel $|x-y|^{-s}$ (resp. $-\log|x-y|$) in a series of Gegenbauer (ultraspherical) polynomials, then applying summation by parts (Abel summation) together with positive-definiteness properties of the partial sums of the resulting inner-product expansion.

Problem: Construct resummation techniques applied to the Gegenbauer expansion of the Riesz and logarithmic kernels on $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$ that yield strictly sharper lower bounds (or higher-order terms in the asymptotic expansion) for $\mathcal{E}_s(N)$ and $\mathcal{E}_{\log}(N)$ than those produced by the summation-by-parts and inner-product-expansion approach. Equivalently, determine whether more efficient resummation methods than summation by parts exist for this class of energy asymptotics.
status_search_result: The question is part of a recent open-problems collection. While substantial work exists on next-order asymptotics for minimal Riesz and logarithmic energies on spheres (Brauchart–Hardin–Saff conjectures, Bétermin–Sandier–Serfaty renormalized-energy methods, Lauritsen's recent results on the logarithmic sphere case), no source found provides a resummation technique improving systematically on summation by parts in the Gegenbauer expansion approach. The status is best classified as open.

paper_title: Open problems UP24
context_brief: Dimension lower bound for equilibrium support
original_question: Let C⊂R^d be a compact convex body, and let μ_eq minimize the Riesz s-energy on C. For convex polytopes such as the hypercube Q^d, known results imply bounds s ≤ dim(supp(μ_eq)) ≤ q−1 when supp(μ_eq) is contained in the union of (q−1)-dimensional faces. Can the lower bound in this dimension estimate be improved?
self_contained_problem:
Let $C \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a compact convex body, and for a parameter $s \in (0,d)$ (or more generally in the range for which the Riesz $s$-energy is well-defined) consider the Riesz $s$-energy functional
$$ I_s(\mu) \;=\; \iint \frac{1}{\|x-y\|^s}\,d\mu(x)\,d\mu(y) $$
defined on Borel probability measures $\mu$ supported in $C$. Let $\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}$ denote the unique minimizer of $I_s$ over such measures (the $s$-equilibrium measure of $C$), and let $\operatorname{supp}(\mu_{\mathrm{eq}})$ denote its closed support, with $\dim$ denoting Hausdorff dimension.

Suppose $C$ is a convex polytope, for example the hypercube $Q^d = [-1,1]^d$, and suppose it is known that $\operatorname{supp}(\mu_{\mathrm{eq}})$ is contained in the union of the $(q-1)$-dimensional faces of $C$ for some integer $1 \le q \le d$. Then one has the dimension estimate
$$ s \;\le\; \dim\bigl(\operatorname{supp}(\mu_{\mathrm{eq}})\bigr) \;\le\; q-1. \tag{$\ast$}$$

Can the lower bound $s \le \dim(\operatorname{supp}(\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}))$ in $(\ast)$ be improved? That is, find a strictly larger function $f(s,d,q) > s$ such that, under the above hypotheses, $\dim(\operatorname{supp}(\mu_{\mathrm{eq}})) \ge f(s,d,q)$, or prove that no such improvement is possible.
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem by Ryan Matzke asking to improve the lower bound in the support-dimension estimate for Riesz s-energy minimizers on convex polytopes such as the hypercube. Recent related work by Matzke and collaborators (e.g., the 2024 paper on Riesz energy with a radial external field) addresses related dimension-reduction phenomena but does not provide an improved lower bound in the polytope setting. No published resolution was located.

paper_title: Open problems UP24
context_brief: Equilibrium support on non-polytope convex bodies
original_question: For compact convex bodies with lower-dimensional faces, beyond hypercubes and more generally beyond convex polytopes, can one obtain analogous results describing how the geometry of the body forces the support of the Riesz-energy equilibrium measure onto lower-dimensional faces? In particular, can this be done for bodies such as the Reuleaux triangle?
self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. For a parameter $s \in \mathbb{R}$, the (generalized) Riesz $s$-kernel on $\mathbb{R}^d$ is
$$ k_s(x,y) = \begin{cases} \|x-y\|^{-s} & \text{if } s>0, \\ -\log\|x-y\| & \text{if } s=0, \\ -\|x-y\|^{-s} & \text{if } s<0, \end{cases} $$
and the Riesz $s$-energy of a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on a compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is
$$ I_s(\mu) = \iint_{K\times K} k_s(x,y)\, d\mu(x)\, d\mu(y). $$
For $s$ in a range where $I_s$ is bounded below and lower-semicontinuous on probability measures supported in $K$, there exists a (unique, under standard convexity hypotheses) equilibrium measure $\mu_K^s$ minimizing $I_s$ over all Borel probability measures supported in $K$.

It is known that for the unit cube $K=[0,1]^d$ (and, more generally, for various convex polytopes), the support of the Riesz equilibrium measure $\mu_K^s$ is forced, for appropriate ranges of $s$, to lie on lower-dimensional faces of $K$ (e.g., on the boundary, or on faces of strictly smaller dimension than $d$).

Problem. Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a compact convex body that is not a convex polytope but possesses lower-dimensional faces (faces of dimension strictly less than $d-1$ in the boundary). Develop analogues of the polytope-case results that describe how the geometry of $K$ forces the support of the Riesz $s$-equilibrium measure $\mu_K^s$ to be contained in (or to concentrate on) lower-dimensional faces of $K$, and identify the ranges of $s$ for which this dimension reduction occurs. As a concrete test case, carry out this analysis for the planar Reuleaux triangle, i.e., the intersection of three closed disks of radius $r$ whose centers form an equilateral triangle of side length $r$.
status_search_result: A web search for related work on Riesz equilibrium measures and the support's concentration on lower-dimensional faces of convex bodies (with the Reuleaux triangle as a test case) did not turn up any paper resolving the question. Recent work by Matzke and collaborators addresses related questions (e.g., when the support is a sphere under a radial external field, and Riesz energy on cubes), but no analogue for general non-polytopal convex bodies with lower-dimensional faces (such as the Reuleaux triangle) appears to be available, suggesting the question remains open.

paper_title: Open problems UP24
context_brief: Support size from delayed negative coefficients
original_question: Let κ:[−1,1]→R have a Gegenbauer expansion with some negative coefficients c_ℓ, all occurring only in degrees ℓ>N for a large N. If the associated energy I_κ has a discrete minimizer μ*, what can be said about the size of the support of μ*?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{d-1}\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be the unit sphere ($d\ge 2$), and for a fixed parameter $\lambda=(d-2)/2$ let $\{C_\ell^{\lambda}\}_{\ell\ge 0}$ denote the Gegenbauer (ultraspherical) polynomials, normalized so that the sequence $\{C_\ell^{\lambda}(t)\}_{\ell\ge 0}$ forms an orthogonal basis of $L^2([-1,1], (1-t^2)^{\lambda-1/2}\,dt)$. Recall the classical theorem of Schoenberg: a continuous function $\kappa:[-1,1]\to\mathbb{R}$ is positive definite on $S^{d-1}$ if and only if its Gegenbauer expansion
$$\kappa(t)=\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty} c_\ell\, C_\ell^{\lambda}(t)$$
has all coefficients $c_\ell\ge 0$.

For a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $S^{d-1}$, define the energy
$$I_\kappa(\mu)=\iint_{S^{d-1}\times S^{d-1}} \kappa(\langle x,y\rangle)\,d\mu(x)\,d\mu(y).$$
Call $\mu^{*}$ a discrete minimizer of $I_\kappa$ if $\mu^{*}$ minimizes $I_\kappa$ over all Borel probability measures on $S^{d-1}$ and $\mathrm{supp}(\mu^{*})$ is a finite set.

Suppose $\kappa$ has a Gegenbauer expansion in which every negative coefficient $c_\ell<0$ occurs only at indices $\ell>N$ for some large integer $N$, while $c_\ell\ge 0$ for all $\ell\le N$. Assuming $I_\kappa$ admits a discrete minimizer $\mu^{*}$, derive quantitative information about $|\mathrm{supp}(\mu^{*})|$ in terms of $N$ (and the dimension $d$). In particular, can one give a lower bound on $|\mathrm{supp}(\mu^{*})|$ that grows with $N$?
status_search_result: The problem is posed by Bilyk in a recent open-problems collection (UP24). Related work by Bilyk and collaborators establishes existence of discrete minimizers and the empty-interior property of supports when the potential is not positive definite, but no quantitative bound on the support size from "delayed" negative Gegenbauer coefficients appears in the literature. No solution was located in the search.

paper_title: Open problems UP24
original_question: Let Ω be either a sphere S^d or a projective space FP^d equipped with a distance ρ equivalent to the geodesic distance, and let S(Ω) be the set of s for which the uniform probability measure σ minimizes the Riesz energy I_s. If σ minimizes I_{s*} for some s*>0, does it follow that σ also minimizes I_s for every s with s*<s<d? Equivalently, must S(Ω) remain connected in the positive-s regime?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega$ be either the unit sphere $S^d \subset \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ or a projective space $\mathbb{F}P^d$ (with $\mathbb{F} \in \{\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}, \mathbb{H}\}$, or the Cayley plane when $d=2$, $\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{O}$), and let $\rho$ be a metric on $\Omega$ that is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to the geodesic distance. Let $\sigma$ denote the unique normalized Riemannian (uniform) probability measure on $\Omega$. For a real parameter $s$, define the Riesz $s$-energy of a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ by
$$I_s(\mu) = \iint_{\Omega \times \Omega} \rho(x,y)^{-s}\, d\mu(x)\, d\mu(y),$$
with the usual convention for $s\le 0$ (replacing $\rho^{-s}$ by $-\rho^{-s}$ or using logarithmic kernels at $s=0$). Define
$$S(\Omega) = \{\, s \in \mathbb{R} : \sigma \text{ minimizes } I_s \text{ over all Borel probability measures on } \Omega \,\}.$$
Suppose there exists $s^* > 0$ such that $\sigma$ is a minimizer of $I_{s^*}$. Must $\sigma$ then be a minimizer of $I_s$ for every $s$ with $s^* < s < d$? Equivalently, must the set $S(\Omega) \cap (0, d)$ be connected (i.e., an interval)?
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem by Peter Grabner in a recent collection of open problems. A web search did not turn up a published resolution; related recent work (e.g., on geodesic-distance Riesz energy on projective spaces) studies the structure of $S(\Omega)$ but does not establish connectedness of its positive part. The status appears to be open.

paper_title: Open problems UP24
original_question: Find a class of nonnegative majorants μ on [−1,1] for which the associated snake polynomials have a Chebyshev expansion whose coefficients are either all nonnegative or sign-alternating.
self_contained_problem:
Let μ : [−1, 1] → [0, ∞) be a nonnegative function (a "majorant"). For each integer n ≥ 1, an associated "snake polynomial" of degree n is a real algebraic polynomial P_n of degree n which is extremal in the sense that it oscillates between ±μ on [−1, 1]: there exist points −1 ≤ x_0 < x_1 < … < x_n ≤ 1 such that P_n(x_k) = (−1)^{n−k} μ(x_k) for k = 0, 1, …, n (so the graph of P_n weaves like a snake between the curves y = μ(x) and y = −μ(x)). Each such polynomial admits a unique expansion
P_n(x) = Σ_{k=0}^{n} a_{n,k} T_k(x),
where T_k denotes the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind of degree k.

Problem: Identify a class C of nonnegative majorants μ on [−1, 1] such that, for every μ ∈ C and every n ≥ 1, the Chebyshev coefficients {a_{n,k}}_{k=0}^{n} of the associated snake polynomial P_n are either all nonnegative or alternate in sign (i.e., (−1)^{n−k} a_{n,k} ≥ 0 for all k).

paper_title: Open problems UP24
original_question: In Prosanov’s upper-bound method for the chromatic number χ(S^{d−1}(R)) of a Euclidean sphere of radius R>√5/2, is there a better choice of the Step 1 configuration—a kissing configuration of spherical caps whose Voronoi tiling is later shrunk and recolored—that leads to a strictly improved upper bound for χ(S^{d−1}(R))?
self_contained_problem:
For a real number $R>0$ and integer $d\ge 2$, let $S^{d-1}(R)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:\|x\|=R\}$ denote the Euclidean sphere of radius $R$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The chromatic number $\chi(S^{d-1}(R))$ is the smallest integer $k$ such that there exists a coloring $c:S^{d-1}(R)\to\{1,\dots,k\}$ with $c(x)\neq c(y)$ whenever $\|x-y\|=1$.

Prosanov's covering/recoloring method produces upper bounds on $\chi(S^{d-1}(R))$ for $R>\sqrt5/2$ by the following two-step procedure:
1. (Step 1) Choose a finite kissing configuration of congruent spherical caps on $S^{d-1}(R)$ (i.e. caps with pairwise disjoint interiors that are tangent in a prescribed pattern), and form the spherical Voronoi tiling associated to the centers of these caps.
2. (Step 2) Slightly shrink the Voronoi cells and assign colors to the shrunken pieces in such a way that no two points at Euclidean distance exactly $1$ receive the same color; the number of colors used yields an upper bound on $\chi(S^{d-1}(R))$.

Question: For $R>\sqrt5/2$, does there exist a choice of the Step 1 kissing configuration of spherical caps, different from the standard one used in Prosanov's method, whose Voronoi-tiling-based recoloring produces a strictly better upper bound on $\chi(S^{d-1}(R))$ than the currently known bound obtained by this method?
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem attributed to D. Cherkashin in a recent open-problems collection. Web searches reveal Prosanov's 2018 paper "Chromatic numbers of spheres" (arXiv:1711.03193) introducing the method, and subsequent works on chromatic numbers of 2-spheres, but no published improvement of the Step 1 kissing configuration was located. The status appears to remain open.

original_question: Let n be a positive integer, and let A1, ..., An be self-adjoint real n x n matrices with spectral norms bounded by 1 (that is, ||Ai|| <= 1 for every i). Does there exist a universal constant C > 0 such that one can always choose signs epsilon1, ..., epsilonn in {+1, -1} so that the operator norm of the signed sum is bounded by C*sqrt(n): ||sum_{i=1}^n epsiloni Ai|| <= C*sqrt(n)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\|\cdot\|$ denote the spectral (operator) norm on real $n\times n$ matrices. Determine whether there exists a universal constant $C>0$ with the following property: for every positive integer $n$ and every choice of self-adjoint real $n\times n$ matrices $A_1,\dots,A_n$ satisfying $\|A_i\|\le 1$ for all $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, there exist signs $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_n\in\{+1,-1\}$ such that
$$\Big\|\sum_{i=1}^n \varepsilon_i A_i\Big\| \le C\sqrt{n}.$$
status_search_result: The Matrix Spencer conjecture remains open in full generality. Bansal, Jiang, and Meka (STOC 2023) resolved it for matrices of rank at most $n/\log^3 n$, and related partial results exist, but the general case for arbitrary self-adjoint matrices with bounded spectral norm is still unresolved.

original_question: For a uniformly random 3-regular graph on n vertices, let E(theta) = (1/2) sum_{i,j=1}^n Aij(1 - cos(theta_i - theta_j)) where A is the adjacency matrix, and call the graph globally synchronizing when all local minima of E are global minima corresponding to constant phase vectors theta_i = c. Is it true that a uniform random 3-regular graph is globally synchronizing with high probability as n -> infinity?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a simple graph on vertex set $\{1,\dots,n\}$ with adjacency matrix $A=(A_{ij})$. For phase angles $\theta=(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n$, define the energy
$$E(\theta)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i,j=1}^{n}A_{ij}\bigl(1-\cos(\theta_i-\theta_j)\bigr).$$
Call $G$ "globally synchronizing" if every local minimum of $E$ on the torus $(\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^n$ is a global minimum, i.e.\ corresponds to a constant phase vector $\theta_i=c$ for all $i$ (so that $E=0$).

Let $G_n$ be a uniformly random 3-regular graph on $n$ vertices (sampled from the set of all simple 3-regular graphs on $n$ labelled vertices, for $n$ even).

Prove or disprove: as $n\to\infty$,
$$\Pr\bigl(G_n\text{ is globally synchronizing}\bigr)\longrightarrow 1.$$
status_search_result: The conjecture appears to be open. Recent work (Abdalla–Bandeira–Kassabov–Souza–Strogatz–Townsend, "Expander graphs are globally synchronizing", 2022) establishes global synchronization for random d-regular graphs only for sufficiently large d (d ≥ 600), and a 2025 paper shows the random graph process is globally synchronizing, but the sparse case d = 3 remains unresolved.

original_question: For the Kuramoto-type global synchronization notion where a graph is globally synchronizing when all local minima of E(theta) = (1/2) sum_{i,j=1}^n Aij(1 - cos(theta_i - theta_j)) are global minima at constant phases, is the following extremal statement true: for every epsilon > 0 there exists n and an n-vertex graph G with minimum degree at least (3/4 - epsilon)n that is not globally synchronizing?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices with adjacency matrix $A=(A_{ij})$. To each vertex $i\in V$ assign a phase $\theta_i\in\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$, and define the Kuramoto energy
$$E(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_n)=\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{i,j=1}^{n}A_{ij}\bigl(1-\cos(\theta_i-\theta_j)\bigr).$$
A constant-phase configuration is one in which $\theta_1=\theta_2=\cdots=\theta_n$; these are the global minima of $E$ (with value $0$). The graph $G$ is said to be globally synchronizing if every local minimum of $E$ is a constant-phase configuration (equivalently, a global minimum).

Decide whether the following statement is true:

For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist an integer $n\ge 1$ and an $n$-vertex graph $G$ with minimum degree $\delta(G)\ge(\tfrac{3}{4}-\varepsilon)n$ such that $G$ is not globally synchronizing.
status_search_result: The conjecture concerns the sharp minimum-degree threshold μ_c for global synchronization of Kuramoto networks. Kassabov, Strogatz and Townsend (2021) proved every graph with minimum degree ≥ 0.75(n−1) is globally synchronizing, giving μ_c ≤ 3/4, and argued that linear stability analysis cannot improve this. The matching lower bound — i.e., the existence, for every ε>0, of graphs of minimum degree ≥ (3/4−ε)n that are not globally synchronizing — remains conjectural and unproven as of recent work (e.g., 2025 papers on expander and threshold graphs).

original_question: Consider multi-frequency group synchronization over SO(2) or over a finite group, with signal elements sampled uniformly from the group and observed through L frequency channels. Determine a scaling L = L_n such that there exists a polynomial-time algorithm that reliably detects the signal as n -> infinity for all signal strengths lambda > lambda_comp,L with lambda_comp,L < 1.
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be either the rotation group $SO(2)$ or a fixed finite group, and let $\{\rho_\ell\}_{\ell\ge 1}$ be a complete list of its nontrivial irreducible unitary representations (the "frequency channels"), with $\rho_\ell : G \to U(d_\ell)$. Fix an integer $n\ge 1$ and let $x_1,\dots,x_n$ be i.i.d. uniformly random elements of $G$ (the hidden signal). For each frequency $\ell \in \{1,\dots,L\}$, one observes the $n\times n$ block matrix
$$Y^{(\ell)} \;=\; \frac{\lambda}{n}\, X^{(\ell)} (X^{(\ell)})^* \;+\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\, W^{(\ell)},$$
where $X^{(\ell)} \in \mathbb{C}^{n d_\ell \times d_\ell}$ has blocks $\rho_\ell(x_i)$, $W^{(\ell)}$ is an independent GUE-type Hermitian noise matrix at scale $\ell$, and $\lambda > 0$ is the signal-to-noise ratio. Under the null hypothesis the observations are pure noise; under the planted hypothesis they follow the model above. The detection task is to test the null against the planted hypothesis with vanishing total error as $n\to\infty$.

For a single frequency ($L=1$), the spectral (PCA) threshold is $\lambda=1$, and it is conjectured (and partially established) that no polynomial-time algorithm achieves reliable detection below this threshold. Allowing the use of $L$ frequency channels jointly, define $\lambda_{\mathrm{comp},L}$ as the infimum of $\lambda$ for which some polynomial-time test reliably detects the signal as $n\to\infty$.

Problem: Determine a scaling $L = L_n$ (as a function of $n$) for which there exists a polynomial-time algorithm (using the observations $Y^{(1)},\dots,Y^{(L_n)}$) that reliably detects the signal for all $\lambda > \lambda_{\mathrm{comp},L_n}$ with $\lambda_{\mathrm{comp},L_n} < 1$; equivalently, exhibit a sub-spectral computationally efficient detection threshold by using sufficiently many frequencies.
status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in a 2025 preprint on multi-frequency group synchronization. A brief web search did not surface a subsequent resolution providing a polynomial-time sub-spectral detector for $SO(2)$ or finite-group synchronization via frequency scaling; the problem appears to remain open.

context_brief: Kikuchi spectral threshold in Tensor PCA
original_question: Fix even tensor order r and integer level ell with n much larger than ell and ell >= r/2. Let M(lambda) be the matrix indexed by ell-subsets I, J of [n], with entries M(lambda)_{I,J} = lambda + Z_{IΔJ} when |IΔJ| = r and 0 otherwise, where Z_S are independent N(0,1) variables for |S| = r. Let lambda^natural_{r,ell} be the eigenvalue pop-out threshold of M(lambda). Is it true that for each fixed r, one has n^{r/4} * lambda^natural_{r,ell} -> 0 as ell -> infinity (after taking n -> infinity)?
self_contained_problem:
Fix an even integer $r \geq 2$ and an integer $\ell \geq r/2$. For each subset $S \subseteq [n] := \{1,2,\dots,n\}$ with $|S| = r$, let $Z_S$ be independent standard Gaussian random variables, and let $\lambda \geq 0$ be a real parameter. Define the symmetric matrix $M(\lambda)$ whose rows and columns are indexed by the $\binom{n}{\ell}$ subsets of $[n]$ of size $\ell$ via
$$
M(\lambda)_{I,J} \;=\; \begin{cases} \lambda + Z_{I \triangle J}, & |I \triangle J| = r, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise,} \end{cases}
$$
where $I \triangle J$ denotes the symmetric difference. Let $\lambda^{\natural}_{r,\ell}(n)$ denote the eigenvalue pop-out threshold of $M(\lambda)$, i.e., the infimum of values $\lambda \geq 0$ such that the top eigenvalue of $M(\lambda)$ separates from the bulk of its spectrum (in the limit $n \to \infty$ with $\ell$ fixed), and write
$$
\lambda^{\natural}_{r,\ell} \;=\; \lim_{n \to \infty} \lambda^{\natural}_{r,\ell}(n)
$$
appropriately rescaled as the limiting threshold. Prove or disprove: for every fixed even integer $r$,
$$
\lim_{\ell \to \infty} \; n^{r/4}\, \lambda^{\natural}_{r,\ell} \;=\; 0,
$$
where the limit $n \to \infty$ is taken first.
status_search_result: The conjecture (a reformulation of a conjecture of Wein–El Alaoui–Moore, 2019) is open in general. Partial results characterize the threshold $\lambda^{\natural}_{r,\ell}$ for even $r$ and $r/2 \leq \ell < 3r/4$ via work of Bandeira, Cipolloni, Schröder, and van Handel (2024), but the full $\ell \to \infty$ limiting statement has not been established.

context_brief: Worst-case normalized discrepancy of sign matrices
original_question: Let disc(A) = inf_{x in {+1,-1}^n} ||Ax||_infinity for A in {+1,-1}^{n x n}. What is the exact value of sup_{n in N} sup_{A in {+1,-1}^{n x n}} (1/sqrt(n)) * disc(A)?
self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$ and a matrix $A \in \{+1,-1\}^{n \times n}$, define the discrepancy
$$\operatorname{disc}(A) \;=\; \inf_{x \in \{+1,-1\}^n} \|Ax\|_\infty,$$
where $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ denotes the maximum absolute coordinate. Determine the exact value of
$$C \;=\; \sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \; \sup_{A \in \{+1,-1\}^{n \times n}} \frac{\operatorname{disc}(A)}{\sqrt{n}}.$$

context_brief: Fast mixing up to beta*=1 in SK model
original_question: Consider the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model with interaction matrix J = beta W where W ~ GOE(n), with an arbitrary external field, and Glauber dynamics for sampling from the Gibbs measure on {+1,-1}^n. Does Glauber dynamics mix in polynomial time for all beta up to the replica-symmetry-breaking threshold beta* = 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $n \ge 1$ and let $W$ be an $n \times n$ matrix drawn from the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (i.e., $W$ is symmetric with $W_{ii} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,2/n)$ and $W_{ij} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1/n)$ for $i < j$, all independent). Fix $\beta > 0$ and an external field vector $h \in \mathbb{R}^n$, and define the Gibbs measure on the hypercube $\{-1,+1\}^n$ by
$$\mu(\sigma) \;=\; \frac{1}{Z}\exp\!\Big(\tfrac{\beta}{2}\,\langle \sigma, W\sigma\rangle + \langle h,\sigma\rangle\Big),$$
where $Z$ is the normalizing partition function. The (single-site) Glauber dynamics is the discrete-time Markov chain on $\{-1,+1\}^n$ that at each step selects a coordinate $i \in \{1,\ldots,n\}$ uniformly at random and resamples $\sigma_i$ from its conditional law under $\mu$ given the remaining coordinates; this chain is reversible with respect to $\mu$.

The replica-symmetry-breaking threshold of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model is $\beta^* = 1$.

Question: Is it true that for every $\beta < 1$ and for every external field $h \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the mixing time of Glauber dynamics for $\mu$ is bounded by a polynomial in $n$ (with high probability over $W$ as $n \to \infty$)?
status_search_result: The problem is open. The best known polynomial mixing-time bound for Glauber dynamics on the SK model holds only up to $\beta < 0.295$ (Anari–Koehler–Vuong, 2024). Alternative samplers based on stochastic localization and Approximate Message Passing achieve sampling (in Wasserstein distance) up to $\beta < 1/2$ (El Alaoui–Montanari–Sellke) and were recently extended by Celentano to all $\beta < 1$, but these are not Glauber dynamics. Whether Glauber dynamics itself mixes in polynomial time up to $\beta^*=1$ remains unresolved.

original_question: For a compact embedded constant-mean-curvature surface in R^3 whose boundary is a planar closed curve C, what hypotheses on the boundary guarantee that the surface lies entirely on one side of the boundary plane, and what additional conclusions hold when C is convex?

context_brief: slab rigidity for H-surfaces with circular boundary
original_question: Let H be nonzero, and let Sigma be a compact H-surface spanning a circle S^1(r). If Sigma is contained in a slab S_w and |H| < 2/w, must Sigma be a spherical cap? If the threshold 2/w is replaced by w*(1/w), must Sigma be a small spherical cap?
self_contained_problem:
Let $H\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$. An $H$-surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a smooth compact orientable immersed surface $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ (possibly with boundary) whose mean curvature is identically equal to the constant $H$. A slab of width $w>0$ is a region $S_w=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb{R}^3 : a\le z\le a+w\}$ between two parallel planes at distance $w$. A spherical cap is a compact piece of a round sphere of radius $1/|H|$ bounded by a circle; it is called a small spherical cap if it is contained in a closed hemisphere of that sphere (equivalently, if its boundary circle is a great circle or smaller and the cap lies on one side).

Let $\Sigma$ be a compact $H$-surface whose boundary $\partial\Sigma$ is a round circle $S^1(r)\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ of radius $r>0$ lying in some plane. Suppose $\Sigma$ is contained in a slab $S_w$ of width $w>0$.

(a) If $|H|<\tfrac{2}{w}$, must $\Sigma$ be a spherical cap?

(b) If the bound $|H|<\tfrac{2}{w}$ is replaced by $|H|< w\cdot\tfrac{1}{w}=1$ (equivalently, by the corresponding sharper threshold $w\!\cdot\!(1/w)$ in place of $2/w$), must $\Sigma$ be a small spherical cap?
status_search_result: The classification of compact CMC surfaces with circular boundary is widely regarded as open: it remains unknown whether spherical caps are the only compact (even embedded) CMC surfaces bounded by a circle. Partial results exist under additional assumptions such as local convexity, embeddedness in a half-space, area bounds, or genus-zero topology, but the slab-rigidity version with thresholds $|H|<2/w$ (cap) and the refined threshold (small cap) has not been resolved in general.

context_brief: convex level curves of cmc graphs
original_question: Suppose Omega is a bounded convex domain in R^2 and u solves the constant-mean-curvature Dirichlet problem div(Du/sqrt(1+|Du|^2)) = 2H in Omega with u = 0 on partial Omega. Determine how the convex level curves of u are distributed as a function of H, and if possible extend Wang's example to the case where Omega is unbounded.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded convex domain, and let $H>0$ be a constant. Consider the constant–mean–curvature Dirichlet problem
$$\operatorname{div}\!\left(\frac{Du}{\sqrt{1+|Du|^2}}\right) = 2H \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial\Omega,$$
whose solution $u\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\overline{\Omega})$ describes a graph of constant mean curvature $H$ spanning $\partial\Omega$. It is known that the level sets $\{u = c\}$ need not all be convex (an example due to X.-J. Wang exhibits non-convex level curves at heights related to $1/(4H)$).

(a) Give a quantitative description, in terms of the value $H$ (and geometric data of $\Omega$), of the distribution of those level curves $\{u = c\}$ that are convex: determine the range of heights $c \in [0, \max_{\overline{\Omega}} u]$ for which $\{u = c\}$ is a convex curve, and characterize the threshold(s) at which convexity is lost.

(b) Extend Wang's counterexample (which produces non-convex level curves of a CMC graph over a bounded convex domain) to the setting where $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ is an unbounded convex domain, or show that no such extension is possible.
category_tag: Constant mean curvature graphs and level sets

original_question: Does every subgroup of a virtually polycyclic group have bounded packing, meaning that for every radius r > 0 there exists N such that any collection of N distinct left cosets contains two cosets whose distance is at least r with respect to a proper left-invariant metric on the ambient group?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a virtually polycyclic group, i.e., a group that contains a polycyclic subgroup of finite index (recall that a group is polycyclic if it admits a finite subnormal series with cyclic factors). Equip $G$ with a proper left-invariant metric $d$ (any two such metrics on a finitely generated group are quasi-isometric, and properness means that balls are finite). For a subgroup $H \le G$ and two left cosets $aH, bH$, define their distance by $d(aH, bH) = \inf\{d(x,y) : x \in aH,\ y \in bH\}$.

A subgroup $H \le G$ is said to have bounded packing in $G$ if for every $r > 0$ there exists a positive integer $N = N(G,H,r)$ such that for any collection $g_1 H, g_2 H, \ldots, g_N H$ of $N$ distinct left cosets of $H$ in $G$, there exist indices $i \ne j$ with $d(g_i H, g_j H) \ge r$.

Prove or disprove: every subgroup $H$ of every virtually polycyclic group $G$ has bounded packing in $G$.
status_search_result: The Hruska–Wise conjecture that every subgroup of a virtually polycyclic group has bounded packing has been established affirmatively in recent work. Partial results (e.g., for polycyclic groups of Hirsch length ≤ 3, and for nilpotent-by-polycyclic groups) appeared earlier, and the full conjecture is reported as settled. Related counterexamples are known for general solvable groups (derived length 3), showing the result does not extend beyond the polycyclic setting.

original_question: In coherent diffraction imaging or ptychography, can one estimate how complex an unknown object is using only its magnitude-only measurements, for example by using existing complexity statistics or by defining new ones that are computable from the measurements before reconstruction?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the setting of coherent diffraction imaging (CDI) and ptychography. An unknown complex-valued object $O:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{C}$ is illuminated by one or more coherent probes, and the detector records only the squared magnitudes of the resulting far-field (Fraunhofer) diffraction patterns. In CDI a single magnitude measurement $I(\mathbf{q})=|\mathcal{F}\{P\cdot O\}(\mathbf{q})|^2$ is collected, where $\mathcal{F}$ denotes the Fourier transform and $P$ is the illumination function; in ptychography a set of such measurements $\{I_j(\mathbf{q})=|\mathcal{F}\{P(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r}_j)\cdot O(\mathbf{r})\}(\mathbf{q})|^2\}_j$ is collected over overlapping probe positions $\{\mathbf{r}_j\}$.

Define the "complexity" of the object $O$ as a quantitative measure of its structural intricacy (for example, its information content, sparsity in some basis, total variation, effective number of degrees of freedom, or any other statistic capturing how difficult $O$ is to represent or reconstruct). 

Problem: Identify or design a statistic $\mathcal{C}$ that takes as input only the magnitude-only measurements $\{I_j\}$ (i.e., is computable directly from the diffraction data, before any phase-retrieval reconstruction of $O$) and provides a reliable estimate of the complexity of the underlying object $O$. Equivalently, determine which existing complexity statistics defined on objects can be approximated, or which new statistics can be defined, purely from the recorded intensities, and analyze their relationship to standard object-domain complexity measures.
category_tag: Phase retrieval and coherent diffraction imaging
status_search_result: No established statistic for estimating object complexity directly from magnitude-only CDI/ptychography measurements (prior to reconstruction) was found in the literature. Existing work focuses on reconstructing the object and then assessing its complexity, rather than predicting complexity from raw intensity data. The question appears to be an open research direction.

original_question: How does the intrinsic complexity of an object manifest itself during phase-retrieval reconstruction, and what quantitative effect does that complexity have on the convergence rate of reconstruction algorithms such as gradient-descent methods?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the phase retrieval problem: given measurements $y_k = |\langle a_k, x\rangle|^2$ for $k=1,\ldots,m$, where $\{a_k\}\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ is a known measurement ensemble and $x\in\mathbb{C}^n$ is an unknown signal, one seeks to recover $x$ (up to a global phase) by minimizing a nonconvex loss such as
$$ f(z) = \frac{1}{m}\sum_{k=1}^m \bigl(|\langle a_k, z\rangle|^2 - y_k\bigr)^2 $$
via iterative algorithms (e.g., gradient descent, Wirtinger flow, or related first-order schemes producing iterates $z_{t+1} = z_t - \eta\,\nabla f(z_t)$).

Introduce a quantitative notion of intrinsic complexity $\mathcal{C}(x)$ of the signal $x$ — for instance the effective sparsity, the support size, the Kolmogorov / description complexity, the entropy of its modulus distribution, or the number of distinct structural features in a real-space representation of $x$ (e.g., when $x$ encodes an image or a density).

Problem. Quantify how the complexity $\mathcal{C}(x)$ of the unknown object enters the reconstruction dynamics. Specifically:

(a) Establish a precise mechanism by which the complexity of $x$ manifests itself during the iterative reconstruction (for example through the local curvature of $f$ near $x$, the size of basins of attraction, the magnitude of spurious critical points, or the conditioning of the linearization of the phase-retrieval map at $x$).

(b) Derive explicit bounds of the form
$$ \|z_t - e^{i\theta_t} x\| \le \Phi\bigl(\mathcal{C}(x),\, m,\, n,\, t\bigr) $$
that exhibit the dependence of the convergence rate of the algorithm on $\mathcal{C}(x)$, and determine whether this dependence is necessary (matching lower bounds) or only sufficient.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction concerning how object complexity affects the convergence rate of iterative phase-retrieval algorithms. While convergence rates for Wirtinger flow and related gradient methods have been established in terms of measurement counts and conditioning, a general quantitative theory linking an intrinsic complexity measure of the signal to the convergence rate appears unresolved in the literature.

original_question: Suppose an object is modeled as a sum of translated feature measures drawn from an application-dependent admissible feature set E, together with a background term. When the admissible feature set E is not known in advance, how can one efficiently determine or learn that set in a reliable and interpretable way?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following inverse-problem setup. An object of interest is modeled as a measure of the form
  μ = Σ_{j=1}^N (δ_{x_j} ∗ f_j) + b,
where each x_j ∈ ℝ^d is an unknown translation, each f_j is an unknown "feature" drawn from a prescribed admissible feature set E (a family of measures or functions on ℝ^d encoding the elementary building blocks of the object, such as templates of components), and b is an unknown background term belonging to a prescribed background class. From measurements of μ (for instance, magnitude-only Fourier measurements or other application-specific data), one would like to recover the locations x_j, the features f_j ∈ E, and the background b.

The admissible set E depends on the application and is, in general, not specified a priori. Devise an efficient, reliable, and interpretable strategy to determine or learn the admissible feature set E itself from data, in such a way that the resulting decomposition of μ into translated features from E plus background is well-posed and faithful to the underlying application.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a May 2025 survey of selected open problems in phase retrieval. No subsequent work resolving it was located in the search.

context_brief: uniqueness and stability of parametrized models
original_question: For the parametrized object model in which the object is expressed using feature weights, feature types, and feature locations, can one prove uniqueness and stability guarantees for recovering those parameters from phaseless measurements, and what sufficient assumptions would make such guarantees valid?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{E}$ be a fixed family of admissible "feature" templates, where each $\mu \in \mathcal{E}$ is a (complex-valued) tempered distribution or finite measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Consider the parametrized class of objects
$$f = \sum_{j=1}^{N} a_j \, \tau_{t_j} \mu_j,$$
where:
- $N \in \mathbb{N}$ is the number of features,
- $\mu_j \in \mathcal{E}$ are the feature types,
- $t_j \in \mathbb{R}^d$ are the feature locations, and $\tau_{t_j}$ denotes translation by $t_j$, i.e., $(\tau_{t_j}\mu_j)(x) = \mu_j(x - t_j)$,
- $a_j \in \mathbb{C}$ are the feature weights.

Suppose $f$ is observed only through phaseless (intensity) measurements, i.e., through the squared modulus of its Fourier transform
$$\mathcal{M}(f)(\xi) = |\hat f(\xi)|^2, \qquad \xi \in \mathbb{R}^d,$$
or, more generally, through $|\langle f, \varphi_\alpha\rangle|^2$ for a prescribed measurement family $\{\varphi_\alpha\}_{\alpha \in A}$.

Determine sufficient conditions on the feature dictionary $\mathcal{E}$, on the configuration $\{(a_j,\mu_j,t_j)\}_{j=1}^N$ (for example, separation of the locations $t_j$, linear independence properties of $\{\tau_{t_j}\mu_j\}$, genericity or non-degeneracy of the weights $a_j$, bounds on $N$), and on the measurement family under which the following hold:

(i) **Uniqueness:** the parameters $(N, \{a_j\}, \{\mu_j\}, \{t_j\})$ are uniquely determined by $\mathcal{M}(f)$, up to the unavoidable global symmetries of the phaseless problem (global phase, global translation, and reflection/conjugation).

(ii) **Stability:** there exists a constant $C > 0$ and a metric $d_{\text{par}}$ on the parameter space such that, for any two admissible parameter tuples $\theta, \theta'$ producing objects $f_\theta, f_{\theta'}$,
$$d_{\text{par}}(\theta,\theta') \;\le\; C \, \| \mathcal{M}(f_\theta) - \mathcal{M}(f_{\theta'}) \|,$$
modulo the same symmetries.

Formulate and prove such uniqueness and stability guarantees, identifying explicit sufficient conditions.
category_tag: phase retrieval and parametric inverse problems
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem (Question 4.3) in a 2025 survey on phase retrieval for parametrized object models. No subsequent work establishing uniqueness and stability guarantees in the stated generality was located.
status_evidence: [{"title": "arXiv:2505.15351", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.15351", "snippet": "Survey on phase retrieval; poses Question 4.3 about uniqueness and stability of the parametrized object model with feature weights, types, and locations.", "claim": "The problem is explicitly listed as an open question; no resolution found."}]

original_question: In the discretized affine phase-retrieval formulation derived from the sparse crystallographic model, how many probe shifts are needed to guarantee unique recovery of the unknown feature weights a_j and locations t_j from the resulting phaseless measurements?
self_contained_problem:
Fix integers $n \geq 1$ and $N \geq 1$. Consider a one-dimensional discrete object on $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ of the sparse "crystallographic" form
$$\mathbf{f} = \mathbf{1} + \sum_{j=1}^{N} a_j\, \mathbf{e}_{t_j},$$
where $\mathbf{1}$ is the constant vector with all entries equal to $1$, the locations $t_1,\dots,t_N \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ are distinct, the weights $a_1,\dots,a_N \in \mathbb{C}$ are of the form $a_j = e^{i\omega_j}-1$ with $\omega_j \in \mathbb{R}$, and $\mathbf{e}_t$ denotes the standard basis vector concentrated at position $t$.

Let $\mathbf{w} \in \mathbb{C}^n$ be a fixed known probe vector, let $F$ denote the normalized discrete Fourier transform on $\mathbb{C}^n$, and for $r \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ let $S_r$ denote the cyclic shift operator $(S_r \mathbf{w})_t = \mathbf{w}_{t-r}$. For a set of probe shifts $R \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, the phaseless measurements are
$$\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{f})(r,k) \;=\; \left| (F\mathbf{w})_k \;+\; \sum_{j=1}^{N} \frac{a_j}{\sqrt{n}}\, (S_r \mathbf{w})_{t_j}\, e^{-2\pi i k (t_j - r)/n} \right|^{2}, \qquad r \in R,\ k \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}.$$

Determine the minimum cardinality $|R|$ (and characterize the configurations of probe shifts $R$) that guarantees unique recovery of the unknown parameters $\{(a_j, t_j)\}_{j=1}^{N}$ from the measurements $\{\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{f})(r,k) : r \in R,\ k \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}\}$.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a 2026 survey of selected open problems in phase retrieval (arXiv:2505.15351), with no published resolution located in the related sparse / crystallographic phase retrieval literature.

original_question: Suppose a generative prior is used to reconstruct a signal by solving a latent-space inverse problem and the resulting solution is z-tilde. Can one detect, or even quantify, the reconstruction bias |G(z-tilde) - f_0| between the generated reconstruction and the true signal, especially when the true signal may lie outside the generative model’s range because of imperfections or defects?
self_contained_problem:
Let $G:\mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}^n$ be a (typically nonlinear) generative model whose image $\mathcal{R}(G) := \{G(z) : z \in \mathbb{R}^k\}$ is regarded as a low-dimensional prior set of "plausible" signals. Let $A:\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^m$ be a known (typically linear) forward measurement operator, let $f_0 \in \mathbb{R}^n$ be an unknown true signal, and let $y = A f_0 + \eta \in \mathbb{R}^m$ be a measurement, where $\eta$ is noise. Consider the latent-space reconstruction
$$\tilde z \;\in\; \arg\min_{z \in \mathbb{R}^k}\; \|A\circ G(z) - y\|_2^2,$$
and define the reconstruction bias
$$\mathrm{Bias}(\tilde z;f_0) \;:=\; \|G(\tilde z) - f_0\|.$$
Crucially, the true signal $f_0$ is not assumed to lie in $\mathcal{R}(G)$ (e.g., $f_0$ may contain defects or anomalies not represented by the generative model).

Problem. Devise a procedure that, using only the generator $G$, the operator $A$, the measurement $y$, and the computed minimizer $\tilde z$ (and not the unknown $f_0$), either (a) detects whether the bias $\|G(\tilde z) - f_0\|$ is significantly nonzero (e.g., flags that $f_0 \notin \mathcal{R}(G)$ or that the reconstruction fails to capture $f_0$), or (b) provides a provable quantitative estimate or bound on $\|G(\tilde z) - f_0\|$.
status_search_result: The question of detecting or quantifying the bias $\|G(\tilde z) - f_0\|$ when the true signal lies outside the range of the generative prior is the subject of ongoing research. Recent work proposes partial approaches: invertible generative models eliminate representation error by construction, error analyses bound the gap between approximate and true posteriors in Bayesian formulations, and distribution-shift uncertainty estimators correlate well with reconstruction error on out-of-distribution inputs. However, no general method is known that, given only $G$, $A$, $y$, and $\tilde z$, certifies or sharply quantifies the bias for arbitrary $f_0 \notin \mathcal{R}(G)$; the problem appears to remain open in this general form.

original_question: Can one design an efficient algorithm for solving the generic optimization problem that combines the forward operator with a model map and weighted regularization, prove convergence guarantees for that algorithm, and understand its robustness to different noise models and to bias from the generative approximation, including how the regularization parameter should be adjusted during the iterations when the signal-to-noise ratio is unknown?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $A:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m_{\ge 0}$ be a (possibly nonlinear) forward measurement operator, for instance the phase-retrieval operator $A(x)=(|\langle a_i,x\rangle|^2)_{i=1}^m$ for given sampling vectors $a_1,\dots,a_m\in\mathbb{C}^n$. Let $G:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{C}^n$ be a (typically nonlinear and non-convex) model map, e.g.\ a trained generative network, that produces approximate signals from a low-dimensional latent code $z\in\mathbb{R}^k$. Let $z_0\in\mathbb{R}^k$ be a target latent code, write the approximation bias $b:=G(z_0)-f_0$ where $f_0\in\mathbb{C}^n$ is the true signal, and assume the observed data are
$$y \;=\; A(f_0) + \varepsilon \;\in\;\mathbb{R}^m,$$
where $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{R}^m$ is a noise vector (Gaussian, Poisson, or otherwise).

Reconstruction problem. Given a data-fidelity loss $\mathcal{L}$, a weighted regularizer $\mathcal{R}_W$ on the latent space depending on a positive weight matrix or schedule $W$, and a regularization parameter $\lambda>0$, consider the optimization problem
$$\min_{z\in\mathbb{R}^k}\; \mathcal{L}\bigl(A(G(z)),\,y\bigr) \;+\; \lambda\,\mathcal{R}_W(z). \qquad(\star)$$

Tasks. 
(1) Design an iterative algorithm that solves $(\star)$ efficiently and prove convergence guarantees for it (e.g.\ convergence of iterates or of objective values, with explicit rates) under suitable assumptions on $A$, $G$, $\mathcal{L}$, and $\mathcal{R}_W$.

(2) Establish quantitative robustness bounds for the reconstructed $\hat z$ (and the corresponding signal estimate $G(\hat z)$) in terms of the noise level $\|\varepsilon\|$ and the generative bias $\|G(z_0)-f_0\|$, under different noise models.

(3) Because the signal-to-noise ratio $\|A(f_0)\|/\|\varepsilon\|$ is not known a priori, devise a rule that adapts the regularization parameter $\lambda=\lambda_t$ along the iterations $t=0,1,2,\dots$ so that the algorithm attains the same (or near-optimal) convergence and robustness guarantees as if the optimal $\lambda$ were known in advance.
status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a May 2025 survey of selected open problems in phase retrieval. No subsequent work resolving all three aspects (efficient algorithm with convergence proof, robustness under varying noise models and generative bias, and adaptive regularization-parameter schedule without known SNR) was located in a web search.
status_evidence: [{"title": "Phasebook: A Survey of Selected Open Problems in Phase Retrieval", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.15351", "snippet": "Survey of open problems in phase retrieval; Problem 5.7 asks for an efficient algorithm with convergence guarantees for the combined forward/generative model, robustness analysis, and adaptive regularization parameter.", "claim": "The problem is stated as an open problem in a recent survey."}]

original_question: For physically structured random measurement matrices built from Fourier transforms and random phase diffusers, such as A = F D F and A = F D_1 F D_2 ... F D_l, can one prove information-theoretic and algorithmic bounds for the weak-recovery threshold alpha_WR and the full-recovery threshold alpha_FR?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the phase retrieval problem in the high-dimensional asymptotic regime: a hidden signal $x^\star \in \mathbb{C}^n$ (drawn, say, uniformly from the complex sphere of radius $\sqrt{n}$) is observed through magnitude-only measurements
$$y = |A x^\star|^2 \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^m,$$
where $A \in \mathbb{C}^{m\times n}$ is a measurement matrix, $m = \alpha n$, and $\alpha>0$ is the oversampling ratio. The squared magnitude is taken entrywise.

For a sequence of estimators $\hat{x}=\hat{x}(y,A)$, define the (normalized) overlap
$$q(\hat{x},x^\star) = \frac{|\langle \hat{x}, x^\star\rangle|}{\|\hat{x}\|\,\|x^\star\|}.$$
The information-theoretic weak-recovery threshold is
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{WR}} = \inf\{\alpha>0 : \exists\,\hat{x}\text{ with }\liminf_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\,q(\hat{x},x^\star)^2 > 0\},$$
and the full-recovery threshold is
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{FR}} = \inf\{\alpha>0 : \exists\,\hat{x}\text{ with }\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\,q(\hat{x},x^\star)^2 = 1\}.$$
Algorithmic counterparts $\alpha_{\mathrm{WR}}^{\mathrm{alg}}$ and $\alpha_{\mathrm{FR}}^{\mathrm{alg}}$ are defined analogously, restricting to polynomial-time estimators.

Now restrict the ensemble of measurement matrices to the physically structured "Fourier–diffuser" families:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] $A = F D F$, where $F$ is the (unitary) discrete Fourier transform on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and $D = \mathrm{diag}(d_1,\dots,d_n)$ with $d_i$ i.i.d.\ uniform on the unit circle in $\mathbb{C}$;
\item[(ii)] More generally, $A = F D_1 F D_2 \cdots F D_\ell$ for a fixed integer $\ell\geq 2$, where each $D_k$ is an independent diagonal matrix of i.i.d.\ uniform unit-modulus phases.
\end{itemize}
(For $m<n$, the construction is followed by sub-sampling $m$ rows; for $m>n$, by independent repetitions.)

Problem: Establish information-theoretic and algorithmic bounds (ideally, sharp values) for the weak-recovery threshold $\alpha_{\mathrm{WR}}$ and the full-recovery threshold $\alpha_{\mathrm{FR}}$ for the phase retrieval problem with measurement matrices drawn from the ensembles (i) and (ii).
category_tag: Phase retrieval thresholds for structured random matrices
status_search_result: Recent works (2024–2025) study structured random phase retrieval with cascaded Fourier–diffuser matrices and demonstrate empirical reconstruction down to oversampling ratios around 2.8 via spectral initialization + gradient descent, but no rigorous information-theoretic or algorithmic determination of the weak- and full-recovery thresholds $\alpha_{\mathrm{WR}}, \alpha_{\mathrm{FR}}$ for the FDF or $FD_1F\cdots D_\ell$ ensembles appears in the literature. The problem is listed among open problems in recent phase-retrieval surveys.

original_question: In event-driven 4D STEM operated in an extremely low-dose regime, where the number of measurements is much larger than the signal dimension but each detector pixel receives very few particles and the measurements are effectively quantized, can one design an efficient phase-retrieval reconstruction method and prove theoretical guarantees for both reconstruction quality and stability in that acquisition model?
self_contained_problem:
Consider the following phase-retrieval measurement model motivated by event-driven four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D STEM) in the extremely low-dose regime. Let x ∈ ℂ^n be an unknown complex signal (representing, e.g., an exit wave or specimen transmission function) to be recovered, and let {a_i}_{i=1}^m ⊂ ℂ^n be a known collection of measurement vectors (modeling probe positions and detector pixels), with m ≫ n. For each i, the expected intensity is λ_i(x) = |⟨a_i, x⟩|^2, and the actual measurement y_i is a quantized (e.g., Poisson-counted) observation of λ_i with very small mean, so that Σ_i λ_i(x) (the total dose) is small and each y_i is typically 0 or 1.

Tasks:
(a) Design a computationally efficient reconstruction algorithm that, given (a_i, y_i)_{i=1}^m, produces an estimate x̂ of x up to a global phase.
(b) Prove theoretical guarantees of the form ‖x̂ − e^{iθ} x‖ ≤ ε(m, n, dose, noise) with high probability under a suitable random or structured model of the measurement vectors, and establish stability of the reconstruction with respect to perturbations and quantization errors in y.

Specify and justify the assumptions on {a_i}, the total dose, and the quantization noise model under which the guarantees hold.
category_tag: phase retrieval from quantized Poisson measurements
status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a recent (2025) work on event-driven 4D STEM reconstruction. Standard phase retrieval theory addresses Gaussian or coded-diffraction measurements with Poisson noise of moderate intensity, but the regime m ≫ n combined with extremely low per-pixel dose (effectively binary/quantized counts) is not covered by existing reconstruction guarantees. No subsequent work establishing such guarantees for this specific acquisition model was located.
status_evidence: [{"title": "arXiv:2505.15351", "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.15351", "snippet": "Open problem on event-driven 4D STEM reconstruction in the low-dose regime, asking for an efficient algorithm with reconstruction and stability guarantees.", "claim": "The problem is stated as an open problem."}]

original_question: Can the subspace-completion approach used in Wigner distribution deconvolution be generalized so that it can recover a signal when an arbitrary number of Fourier coefficients are missing, while still keeping the computational cost reasonable?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $f \in \mathbb{C}^N$ be an unknown signal whose discrete Fourier transform $\hat f \in \mathbb{C}^N$ we wish to recover from intensity-only ptychographic measurements. In Wigner distribution deconvolution (WDD), one collects, for a known window/probe $w \in \mathbb{C}^N$ and a set of translates $\{T_\ell w\}_{\ell}$, the squared moduli $|\langle f, M_k T_\ell w\rangle|^2$, where $M_k$ and $T_\ell$ denote modulation and translation operators. These measurements give access, via a 2D Fourier transform, to entries of the Wigner-type matrix
$$X_{j,k} \;=\; \hat f(j)\,\overline{\hat f(j+k)}\,\cdot\, c_{j,k}(w),$$
where $c_{j,k}(w)$ are known coefficients depending on the window. After deconvolving by the known window factors, one obtains (a subset of) the rank-one matrix $\hat f \hat f^*$, from which $\hat f$ is recovered up to a global phase.

In practice some Fourier coefficients of the window vanish (or are too small to invert stably), so certain off-diagonals of $\hat f \hat f^*$ are missing. The subspace completion (SC) method exploits the rank-one structure of $\hat f \hat f^*$ to recover a small number of missing diagonals by solving a low-dimensional eigenvector problem on accessible blocks. Standard SC is designed for the case where only a few off-diagonals are inaccessible, and its operational cost grows rapidly with the number of missing off-diagonals.

Problem. Design and analyze a generalization of the subspace completion technique that provably recovers $\hat f$ (up to a global phase) from the available entries of $\hat f \hat f^*$ when an arbitrary number of off-diagonals (equivalently, an arbitrary subset of Fourier coefficients of the window) are missing, while keeping the total computational cost reasonable (e.g.\ polynomial in $N$, and ideally near-linear or matching the cost of a small number of FFTs). Provide both an algorithm and conditions on the missing-pattern under which exact or stable recovery is guaranteed.

original_question: For Wigner distribution deconvolution with symmetric or more general windows whose ambiguity factors may vanish, what bandlimit assumptions on the unknown signal are sufficient to ensure unique recovery, and more generally what quantitative relationship links the size and location of the vanishing factors |F[w · S_xi w]_x| to the band-limitedness of the signal?
self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ be an unknown signal and let $w \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ be a known window. For $\xi \in \mathbb{R}^d$, let $S_\xi$ denote the modulation/shift operator and define the windowed correlations $[w \cdot S_\xi w]_x = \overline{w(x)}\, w(x+\xi)$ (the window's ambiguity factor at shift $\xi$, evaluated at $x$). The short-time Fourier transform (STFT) of $f$ with window $w$ is
\[ V_w f(x,\omega) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} f(t)\,\overline{w(t-x)}\, e^{-2\pi i \omega \cdot t}\, dt, \]
and its spectrogram is $|V_w f|^2$. Wigner Distribution Deconvolution (WDD) recovers $f$ (up to a global phase) from $|V_w f|^2$ by inverting, frequency-by-frequency, multiplication by the window ambiguity function $A_w(\xi,\eta) = \mathcal{F}_x[\,\overline{w(\cdot)}\, w(\cdot+\xi)\,](\eta)$. Recovery fails at frequencies where $A_w$ vanishes.

Problem. 
(a) Determine a sufficient bandlimit hypothesis on $f$ (i.e., a condition of the form $\operatorname{supp}\widehat{f} \subseteq \Omega$ for some explicit set $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$) which, in the case of a symmetric window $w$ (so that $A_w$ may have non-trivial zero sets), guarantees that $f$ is uniquely determined (up to a global phase) by its spectrogram $|V_w f|^2$ via the WDD procedure.

(b) More generally, for an arbitrary window $w \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, establish a quantitative relationship between the size and location of the zero set $Z_w = \{(\xi,\eta) : A_w(\xi,\eta) = 0\}$ (where $A_w(\xi,\eta) = \big|\mathcal{F}[w \cdot S_\xi w]_x(\eta)\big|$ vanishes) and the band-limitedness of $f$ that suffices for unique recovery of $f$ from $|V_w f|^2$ through WDD.
status_search_result: Web search did not surface a published resolution of this specific question relating zero sets of the window ambiguity function to bandlimit hypotheses guaranteeing unique recovery via Wigner Distribution Deconvolution. Existing WDD uniqueness results address either non-vanishing ambiguity (generic windows) or specific discrete/aliased settings, and the symmetric-window case with vanishing ambiguity factors remains posed as an open question with no quantitative answer found.

original_question: For sampled short-time Fourier transform phase retrieval of compactly supported or otherwise structured functions, which window functions other than the already analyzed Gaussian or specially constructed simple windows allow recovery up to a global phase from magnitude samples taken on a lattice?
self_contained_problem:
For a window function $w \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, define the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) of $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ by
$$
V_w f(x,\xi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}} f(t)\,\overline{w(t-x)}\,e^{-2\pi i \xi t}\,dt, \qquad (x,\xi) \in \mathbb{R}^2.
$$
Two functions $f, g \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ are said to be equal up to a global phase if there exists $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ with $g = e^{i\alpha} f$. Given a lattice $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ (i.e., a discrete subgroup of full rank), say that the sampled STFT phase retrieval problem with window $w$ on $\Omega$ is solvable on a class $\mathcal{C} \subseteq L^2(\mathbb{R})$ if every $f \in \mathcal{C}$ is uniquely determined, up to a global phase, by the magnitude samples $\{|V_w f(\lambda)| : \lambda \in \Omega\}$.

Characterize the windows $w \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, other than Gaussians, for which there exists a lattice $\Omega$ and a natural class $\mathcal{C}$ (for instance, compactly supported functions, or other structured subclasses of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$) such that the sampled STFT phase retrieval problem with window $w$ on $\Omega$ is solvable on $\mathcal{C}$. In particular, identify general structural conditions on $w$ that guarantee or preclude recovery up to a global phase from lattice magnitude samples.
status_search_result: Recent work establishes a "discretization barrier": for general $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ functions, uniqueness in sampled STFT phase retrieval on any lattice is unachievable regardless of the single window chosen. Workarounds use multi-window Gabor systems, non-lattice sampling sets (e.g., square-root lattices), or restricted function classes. The general question of which single windows admit lattice-based recovery on structured subclasses remains open, with only partial results for Gaussians and special constructed windows.
